assertion.name: Revised PER2 Circadian Phosphoswitch Model
assertion.description: Mechanistic mammalian circadian-clock ODE model embedding competing PER2 phosphorylation fates in the transcription-translation feedback loop. Its FASP-like condition reduces both modeled priming-phosphorylation rates to 10% of their wild-type values, while the 2018 revision explicitly represents CK1epsilon and CK1delta isoform binding, phosphorylation, and carboxyl-terminal-tail regulation.
assertion.base_model: Kim-Forger mammalian circadian clock with the 2015 Zhou-Kim PER2 phosphoswitch
assertion.model_format: Mathematica Notebook (.nb)

modeled_mechanisms.description: The model represents competition between the stabilizing FASP-region phosphorylation route and the degradation-promoting beta-TrCP phosphodegron route, then lowers FASP-route phosphorylation as an S662G-like parameterization.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The 2018 revision assigns physiological priming-site control to CK1delta/epsilon, whereas 2026 knockout and biochemical evidence found no phase-advance phenotype after deletion of CK1delta/epsilon or five other candidate kinases and instead identified MARK2 as physiologically significant at S662. The phosphoswitch competition remains informative, but its enzyme assignment should not be treated as settled human biology. The parameter reduction does not explicitly represent a heterozygous allele or human allele dosage.

readouts.name: Simulated PER2 degradation kinetics
readouts.interpretation: The degradation plateau and subsequent loss of PER2 report competition between the stabilizing FASP route and the degradation route.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The FASP parameterization produces a shorter simulated period and the revision also reproduces the directions of CK1epsilon- and CK1delta-knockout period changes.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Validation is against molecular degradation kinetics and human/mouse period directions, not prospective patient time series. The model omits multicellular SCN coupling, individual light exposure, sleep homeostasis, melatonin output, and social schedules, and therefore does not predict an individual's sleep-onset or wake-time advance.

readouts.name: Simulated free-running circadian period in the FASP condition
readouts.interpretation: The shortened model period reproduces the fast-clock direction of FASPS but is not a quantitative clinical forecast.

variables.name: First CK1 priming-phosphorylation rate
variables.description: PER2 priming-site phosphorylation rate for the first modeled CK1 species; reduced to 10% of wild type in the FASP condition.

variables.name: Second CK1 priming-phosphorylation rate
variables.description: PER2 priming-site phosphorylation rate for the second modeled CK1 species; reduced to 10% of wild type in the FASP condition.

variables.name: PER2 abundance
variables.description: Total modeled PER2 across phosphorylation and binding states.

variables.name: Free-running circadian period
variables.description: Period of the simulated mammalian clock under each genetic condition.

findings.statement: The revised model reproduces the shortened period of FASP humans and mice, the longer period of CK1delta-knockout mice, and negligible period change in CK1epsilon-knockout mice.

assertion.notes: Repository inspected at commit 493a69d40c224b93d975d890277a4d71797aee2c. The repository is linked from the Biomedical Mathematics Group's software catalog and contains the 2015 Simple_Model_Final_Sub.nb and 2018 Math_Model_Code2.nb Mathematica notebooks, but no license or environment manifest. The paper's prose names the two FASP rates kp1/kp2, whereas its parameter table and the archived notebook use kr1/kr2. A smoke test that independently transcribed the published equations and used SciPy BDF integration produced a 23.937-h wild-type period and a 20.012-h period after reducing kr1/kr2 by 90%; direct notebook execution requires proprietary Wolfram software and was not available in the verification environment.

selected_evidence.snippet: While CK1 phosphorylation of PER2 was previously shown to be robust to changes in the cellular environment, our phosphoswitch mathematical model of circadian rhythms shows that the CK1 carboxyl-terminal tail can allow the period of the clock to be sensitive to cellular signaling.

assertion.name: Wearable-Light Circadian Phase Particle-Filter Model
assertion.description: Human physiological circadian model that drives the St. Hilaire light-response process and modified van der Pol pacemaker with each participant's ambulatory wrist-light time series. A particle ensemble spans unknown starting phases and produces a posterior distribution of predicted dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO).
assertion.base_model: St. Hilaire 2007 modification of the Jewett-Forger-Kronauer human circadian pacemaker model
assertion.model_software: MATLAB with R functional principal-component analysis
assertion.model_format: MATLAB/R scripts

modeled_mechanisms.target: Advanced Circadian Phase of Melatonin, Temperature and Sleep Propensity
modeled_mechanisms.description: The participant-specific light history drives a human pacemaker model whose phase is reported as predicted DLMO and compared with an in-laboratory DLMO measurement.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The validation cohorts comprised 56 healthy adults with regular schedules and 32 shift workers, not people with ASPS. Model parameters and light sensitivity were not individually fitted, wrist illuminance is an imperfect proxy for retinal exposure, and validation used one laboratory phase marker per participant. The model estimates phase but does not represent the disorder's PER2, CSNK1D, CRY2, TIMELESS, CACNA1D, or PER3 lesions.

readouts.name: Predicted dim-light melatonin onset
readouts.target: Advanced Circadian Phase of Melatonin, Temperature and Sleep Propensity
readouts.interpretation: Predicted DLMO is a model-derived phase marker compared with laboratory DLMO; an early value would measure advanced phase but has not been validated specifically in ASPS.

findings.statement: Fourteen-day phase estimates showed Lin concordance of 0.93 in the regular schedule cohort and 0.89 in shift workers when all 1,440 starting-phase particles were used.
Longer recordings improved accuracy for regular schedules but did not consistently improve accuracy in shift workers with irregular light diets.

assertion.notes: Repository inspected at commit f953b2c6d4351ff93544248189d6c71ed580938d. It contains MATLAB/R analysis and ODE code but no license, dependency manifest, or participant data. Several scripts contain author-local absolute paths, so the published workflow is not runnable end to end without manual path repair and restricted input data. The model is classified as PHYSIOLOGICAL rather than DIGITAL_TWIN because it assimilates individual light histories and state uncertainty but does not fit individual model parameters or validate counterfactual treatment response.

selected_evidence.snippet: We evaluate the impact of initialization strategy, recording duration, and light exposure characteristics on model performance using wearable data from both individuals on regular schedules and shift workers.

assertion.name: Vanselow PER2 Multisite-Phosphorylation Oscillator
assertion.description: Five-variable ordinary differential equation extension of a Goodwin oscillator that separates PER2 into unphosphorylated, singly phosphorylated, doubly phosphorylated, and nuclear species. The FASPS perturbation reduces the second phosphorylation rate, representing loss of the human PER2 S662 priming site, and tests how competing phosphorylation routes change clock period.
assertion.base_model: Goodwin oscillator
assertion.model_format: Five-variable ordinary differential equation system

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reducing the model's second phosphorylation rate represents loss of the FASPS priming phosphosite and shifts PER2 toward faster nuclear clearance and degradation.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The deliberately minimal oscillator lumps many PER2 phosphosites and interacting proteins into five variables, was parameterized from mouse fibroblast experiments rather than human pacemaker neurons, and does not encode a heterozygous human allele or allele dosage. It also does not establish the identity of the physiological S662 kinase. Later evidence identifies MARK2 rather than the historically assumed CK1delta/epsilon activity as the physiologically significant regulator of this site.

readouts.name: Direction of period change after second-site phosphorylation reduction
readouts.interpretation: A selective reduction of the stabilizing phosphorylation route produces a short period, whereas broader kinase loss can produce the opposite direction; the readout tests the phosphosite logic rather than a complete human sleep phenotype.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Selective attenuation of the FASPS-site phosphorylation route shortens the simulated oscillator period, matching the fast-clock direction measured in familial advanced sleep phase.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model reproduces the direction of the cell-autonomous period change but does not represent SCN network coupling, light entrainment, melatonin, temperature, sleep propensity, or social timing. It therefore cannot by itself predict the magnitude of an individual's phase advance.

readouts.name: Simulated free-running circadian period
readouts.interpretation: A shorter simulated period reports the fast-clock mechanism but not the full clinical advanced-sleep-phase phenotype.

variables.name: PER2 mRNA abundance
variables.description: Transcriptional state inhibited by nuclear PER2 in the Goodwin feedback loop.

variables.name: Doubly phosphorylated PER2 abundance
variables.description: PER2 state produced through the stabilizing phosphorylation route impaired in FASPS.

variables.name: Second-site phosphorylation rate
variables.description: Rate constant reduced to represent the FASPS-associated loss of the nuclear-retention phosphorylation route.

variables.name: Nuclear PER2 abundance
variables.description: Nuclear repressor state closing the modeled transcriptional feedback loop.

variables.name: Free-running circadian period
variables.description: Period of the sustained molecular oscillation under a parameter set.

findings.statement: The model predicts that different PER2 phosphorylation perturbations can drive circadian period in opposite directions.

assertion.notes: The equations and parameters are published in the article and supplement; no maintained standalone source-code repository was identified. The paper reports MATLAB for numerical calculation. This is a conceptual molecular oscillator, not a patient-specific or treatment-planning model.

selected_evidence.snippet: To conceptualize our findings, we use mathematical modeling and predict that differential PER phosphorylation events can result in opposite period phenotypes.

assertion.name: Phillips Coupled Sleep-Wake and Circadian Chronotype Model
assertion.description: Physiological model coupling a neuronal sleep-wake switch, homeostatic sleep pressure, and a circadian pacemaker. Parameter sweeps separate chronotypes driven by sleep-homeostatic kinetics from those driven by intrinsic circadian period and provide a syndrome-level explanation for familial advanced and delayed sleep-phase disorders.
assertion.base_model: Phillips-Robinson sleep-wake switch coupled to a circadian pacemaker
assertion.model_format: Coupled physiological differential-equation model

modeled_mechanisms.description: Intrinsic circadian period is varied independently of sleep-homeostatic production and clearance rates to test which parameter regimes move chronotype and physiological phase markers together.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model is a generic human chronotype model rather than an ASPS genotype model. It does not encode PER2, CSNK1D, CRY2, TIMELESS, CACNA1D, or PER3, and the publication does not calibrate a disease-specific short-period parameter set against an ASPS cohort.

readouts.name: Modeled chronotype response to intrinsic-period variation
readouts.interpretation: A change in sleep timing attributable to the intrinsic-period parameter distinguishes a circadian mechanism from a homeostatic route to morningness; the abstract does not provide a disease-specific effect size.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Advanced Circadian Phase of Melatonin, Temperature and Sleep Propensity
modeled_mechanisms.description: The coupled pacemaker and sleep-wake system links chronotype to the relative timing of sleep and circadian phase markers, supplying a physiological bridge from altered intrinsic period to familial phase disorders.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: This is a conceptual explanation rather than validation against DLMO, temperature, actigraphy, or sleep timing from people with ASPS. It cannot predict an individual's phase advance or treatment response.

readouts.name: Relative timing of sleep and circadian phase markers
readouts.target: Advanced Circadian Phase of Melatonin, Temperature and Sleep Propensity
readouts.interpretation: Co-shifting modeled sleep timing and circadian phase markers represents the circadian subtype of extreme morningness, but the paper does not report a calibrated ASPS phase advance.

variables.name: Chronotype
variables.description: Relative timing of the modeled sleep episode.

findings.statement: The model distinguishes extreme chronotype caused by homeostatic kinetics from chronotype in which circadian phase markers track changes in intrinsic circadian period.

assertion.notes: No exact public code or standard model archive was identified. The model is curated from the paper and is retained as a low-fidelity syndrome-level bridge, not as a patient-specific model or a representation of a known ASPS allele.

selected_evidence.snippet: A physiologically based model is developed by combining models of the sleep-wake switch and circadian pacemaker, providing a means of examining how interactions between these systems affect chronotype.

disease_term.description: A RASopathy characterized by distinctive facial features, short stature, congenital heart defects, and variable developmental delays.

assertion.name: SOS1 R1131K Transfer-Entropy Signaling Model
assertion.description: Information-theoretic model of bidirectional predictive dependence between SOS1 and RAF from simultaneous single-cell membrane-translocation trajectories. A Gaussian covariance approximation estimates time-resolved transfer entropy in wild-type and Noonan-associated SOS1 R1131K cells with or without MEK inhibition, revealing phase-specific effective regulation consistent with feedback changes or shared hidden inputs.
assertion.base_model: Gaussian-approximation transfer-entropy method of Imaizumi et al. 2022
assertion.model_software: Python 3.9.7, Jupyter, NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, and seaborn
assertion.model_format: Jupyter Notebook and CSV single-cell time series

modeled_mechanisms.description: Uses SOS1 and RAF membrane-translocation dynamics to measure how R1131K changes effective information flow through the SOS-RAF signaling system. This is an indirect functional readout of the SOS node; RAS-GTP loading is not measured.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Transfer entropy quantifies predictive dependence and does not identify a unique biochemical path or prove molecular causality; hidden or common inputs can generate backward information flow. The acute EGF experiment uses SOS1-knockout HeLa cells with ectopic Halo-SOS1 and GFP-RAF, retains endogenous SOS2, pools cells across independent measurements, and does not model development or patient phenotypes. The Gaussian approximation is a first-order treatment of noisy, potentially non-Gaussian trajectories.

readouts.name: Early RAF-to-SOS backward transfer entropy
readouts.interpretation: R1131K increases the early backward information-flow peak, indicating an altered effective feedback regime rather than increased RAS-GTP itself.

readouts.name: Late RAF-to-SOS backward transfer entropy
readouts.interpretation: R1131K decreases the late backward information-flow peak without MEK inhibition, showing that the same allele has opposite phase-specific effects.

readouts.name: Late-phase transfer-entropy abnormality after MEK inhibition
readouts.interpretation: Trametinib removed the late-phase abnormality but did not normalize the early phase, so the rescue is explicitly phase-specific.

variables.name: SOS1 membrane-translocation trajectory
variables.description: One-minute single-cell Halo-SOS1 response sequence after EGF stimulation.

variables.name: RAF membrane-translocation trajectory
variables.description: Simultaneously measured single-cell GFP-RAF response sequence.

variables.name: SOS-to-RAF transfer entropy
variables.description: Forward predictive information flow from SOS to RAF.

variables.name: RAF-to-SOS transfer entropy
variables.description: Backward predictive information flow reflecting feedback or shared hidden inputs.

findings.statement: R1131K raises early backward transfer entropy and lowers late backward transfer entropy, revealing a signaling defect not evident from RAF activation or translocation amplitude alone.
Trametinib restores the late-phase transfer-entropy abnormality but not the early-phase abnormality.

assertion.notes: `model_type` is deliberately omitted: information-theoretic network inference fits none of the current enum values and is not a kinetic, machine-learning or Boolean model. The paper-pinned Software Heritage revision is 7ff6a1cfdef5163ae98a663381e12cc4f065d3f6; the mutable repository home is https://github.com/YasushiSako/transfer_entropy_2. That revision has no software-license file; repository HEAD 3467850de2e45dfc2b7766ba4dce0d7af8839a00 only adds the MIT LICENSE. The README licenses the 16 CSV data files under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Curator static inspection confirmed that all wild-type and R1131K, vehicle and MEK-inhibitor CSVs are present. value.name: Populations of Human Ventricular Action Potential Models (Passini 2017)
value.description: In silico drug-trial framework in which the O'Hara-Rudy dynamic (ORd) human ventricular action potential model is expanded into a population of 1,213 control models whose ionic-current conductances vary, retaining only models consistent with human experimental recordings. Reference compounds are applied as multi-channel pore block (IC50 and Hill coefficient), and the occurrence of repolarization abnormalities across the population is used to predict clinical torsade de pointes risk. It models drug-induced (acquired) proarrhythmia in wild-type cells, not the inherited channel defects that define this entry; it is linked here through the drug-unmasking node that the two forms share.
value.base_model: O'Hara-Rudy ORd human ventricular action potential model (PMID:21637795)

assertion.statement: Repolarization abnormalities in the model population predicted clinical torsade de pointes risk for 62 reference compounds with 89% accuracy.

assertion.name: Virtual Multiple Sclerosis Patient Whole-Brain Model
assertion.description: Subject-specific delayed whole-brain model that couples 84 noisy Stuart-Landau oscillators according to each participant's DTI-derived connectome. Simulation-based Bayesian inference uses source-reconstructed MEG alpha-spectrum features to estimate a global coupling parameter and one average whole-brain conduction velocity for each participant.
assertion.base_model: Delayed Stuart-Landau subject-specific whole-brain network
assertion.model_format: Python/C++ source and Jupyter notebooks

modeled_mechanisms.description: The inverse model treats slower large-scale signal propagation as a functional consequence of myelin damage and infers an individual average conduction velocity from the participant's connectome and MEG spectrum.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model does not simulate immune attack, myelin loss, lesion formation, remyelination, or axonal injury. It collapses spatially heterogeneous conduction into one homogeneous whole-brain velocity, and alpha-spectrum changes can also arise from excitation/inhibition balance, 1/f structure, or thalamic-loop changes. The evidence comes from 18 patients and 20 controls at one site; EDSS was available for 17 patients, and no external or longitudinal validation cohort was used.

readouts.interpretation: A lower inferred velocity is interpreted as the aggregate functional effect of myelin damage, not a direct measurement of lesion-wise demyelination.

variables.description: Peak amplitude of the median 8-13-Hz power spectral density.

variables.description: Area under the median power spectral density from 8 to 13 Hz.

findings.statement: Inferred average conduction velocity was lower in the 18-person MS group than in 20 controls, while global coupling did not differ.
Inferred conduction velocities were stronger predictors of clinical disability than structural damage in this cohort.

assertion.notes: Curator inspection on 2026-08-20 used repository commit 67cb165d2631f73cfae79643accf7bae3e7b4ef1 (also tagged v1.0). No LICENSE file or license grant was present; an MIT classifier in setup.py is not sufficient to license the code. The repository contains the delayed Stuart-Landau forward solver and an SBI demonstration, but not the clinical connectomes, MEG inputs, trained posterior, or complete 38-subject analysis. In the curator's smoke test, the default install failed to build the SWIG extension; after a manual build and dependency repairs, a synthetic three-node forward simulation produced finite time series and an alpha-band PSD. Curator comparison also found material paper/code differences in simulation duration, noise scale, priors, alpha band, and feature count. Reproducing the clinical findings therefore requires restricted data and missing workflow components. The paper reports a patent application and calls for larger multicenter replication.

assertion.name: Lesion-Aware Personalized Whole-Brain Conduction-Delay Model
assertion.description: Direct successor to the Virtual Multiple Sclerosis Patient model. It retains each participant's 84-region DTI connectome and noisy Stuart-Landau dynamics but augments distance-derived edge delays based on a shared whole-brain velocity with an additive tract-specific term derived from the fraction of each tract intersecting the participant's FLAIR lesion mask. Simulation-based inference estimates the patient-specific strength of the lesion-to-delay relationship.
assertion.base_model: Virtual Multiple Sclerosis Patient whole-brain model (PMID:38974971)
assertion.model_software: Custom Stuart-Landau simulator with the SBI toolbox

modeled_mechanisms.description: The model maps the fraction of each white-matter tract occupied by a patient-specific lesion to an additional edge-specific conduction delay, then infers a subject-level lesion-effect parameter from MEG spectra.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: FLAIR lesion fraction is an imaging proxy, not a direct measure of myelin thickness, axon diameter, or active inflammation. The model does not generate lesions or simulate immune attack, remyelination, axonal damage, or progression. One scalar gamma applies the same lesion-to-delay rule to all affected tracts, source reconstruction is vulnerable to volume conduction, and alternative mechanisms can alter alpha spectra. The same 18-patient/20-control source cohort as the 2024 study was used, without longitudinal or external validation.

readouts.interpretation: More lesion involvement adds a larger modeled delay on the affected tract; this is a personalized functional proxy rather than direct lesion-wise electrophysiology.

readouts.name: Alpha-spectrum peak amplitude as lesion-effect weight increases
readouts.interpretation: Lower simulated alpha peak amplitude with larger lesion-effect weight is the spectral feature used to invert the patient-specific parameter.

findings.statement: The inferred lesion-to-delay weight correlated inversely with alpha peak power (r=-0.83), whereas total lesion load did not correlate with alpha peak power or the inferred weight.

Adding the inferred lesion-effect parameter to the cross-sectional EDSS model yielded leave-one-out R2=0.29882 and adjusted R2=0.018348, but its coefficient was not statistically significant (p=0.1784).

assertion.notes: A curator search on 2026-08-20 identified no paper-specific code repository or executable model archive, and the clinical inputs are available only on request. Curator inspection found that the open VBI package contains generic Stuart-Landau and SBI components but not this paper's lesion-specific gamma-by-tract formulation, so it is not cited as the model artifact. The article is CC BY 4.0, which licenses the paper rather than an unreleased implementation. Synthetic parameter recovery had slope 0.8 and showed boundary bias. The clinical analysis reuses the small cross-sectional source cohort from the 2024 model; the gamma term was not a statistically significant EDSS predictor, and longitudinal validation is still needed.

assertion.name: UISS-MS Agent-Based Treatment Simulator
assertion.description: Multiscale, multi-compartment agent-based model of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. Its physiology layer represents innate and adaptive immune agents; its MS disease layer represents antigen presentation, Th1/Th17 and B-cell responses, blood-brain-barrier migration, CNS inflammation, and oligodendrocyte loss; and its treatment layers simulate cladribine and ocrelizumab. Retrospective virtual cohorts were selected to match aggregate CLARITY and OPERA trial characteristics and outcomes.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The disease layer explicitly represents cytokine-dependent Th1 and Th17 differentiation, migration across the blood-brain barrier, reactivation in the CNS, and inflammatory interactions with microglia and other immune agents.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The immune rules are a mechanistic abstraction assembled from a conceptual ontology rather than fitted to longitudinal cellular or cytokine data from individual patients. Validation is against aggregate relapse and safety outcomes in selected RRMS-like virtual populations, not direct measurements of Th1/Th17 states. Progressive MS and compartmentalized chronic CNS inflammation are outside the demonstrated validation scope.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Immune-agent interactions drive loss of modeled oligodendrocytes, which is used as the simulation's cellular proxy for myelin injury and relapse.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Demyelination is reduced to oligodendrocyte loss in a simulated 3-mm3 white-matter volume. The model does not resolve myelin ultrastructure, tract-specific conduction, remyelination, or axonal injury, and the oligodendrocyte-loss threshold is not an individualized imaging model.

readouts.name: Oligodendrocyte loss during simulated relapse
readouts.interpretation: Rapid loss of modeled oligodendrocytes is the disease-layer readout for a demyelinating event; treatment benefit appears as fewer such losses.

modeled_mechanisms.description: UISS-MS converts sufficiently large simulated oligodendrocyte-loss events into MRI-detectable relapses, providing a coarse lesion-level output for comparison with clinical-trial relapse data.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: A fixed loss of 50,000 oligodendrocytes is used as the MRI-detection threshold. This is a derived event proxy, not a spatial lesion-growth or MRI-physics model, and it does not reproduce lesion topography, contrast enhancement, immune-cell composition, chronic-active rims, or lesion-wise uncertainty.

readouts.name: MRI-detectable relapse event
readouts.interpretation: An oligodendrocyte-loss event at or above the fixed threshold is counted as one or more MRI-detectable lesions for trial-level relapse analysis.

variables.name: Activated Th17-cell population
variables.description: Modeled Th17 immune-agent population and activation state.

variables.description: Cellular state whose rapid loss represents demyelinating relapse in the simulated white-matter compartment.

variables.name: MRI-detectable lesion event

variables.description: Trial-level relapse-rate output used for OPERA comparison.

variables.description: Treatment-safety output used to grade cladribine-associated lymphocytopenia.

findings.statement: In the OPERA simulations, predicted annualized relapse rates were 0.193 for ocrelizumab versus 0.16 observed and 0.349 for interferon beta-1a versus 0.29 observed; the predicted relative reduction was 45.7% versus 50% in the clinical trial.
Retrospective virtual cohorts reproduced the reported directions of cladribine and ocrelizumab treatment outcomes.

assertion.notes: A curator search on 2026-08-20 identified no public UISS-MS source repository, executable archive, or software license. The article is open access, but that does not license the simulator. Although the authors describe a digital-twin use case, this study had only population-level demographic inputs: thousands of immune repertoires were generated and subsets were selected to match aggregate trial behavior. It therefore does not validate one-to-one patient twins or prospective individual counterfactuals. The CLARITY cohort was used in selection/calibration before the extension analysis, and formal VVUQ and regulatory credibility assessment remained future work.

selected_evidence.snippet: Th17 cells secrete various cytokines, including IL-17, IL-6, IL-21, IL-22, IL-23, and TNF-α. Subsequently, these cells migrate across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to the central nervous system (CNS) under the influence of specific cytokines, namely IL-17, IL-6, and IL-22, as well as IL-23, provided that the inhibitory effects of IL-10 are absent.

value.name: UISS-MS Agent-Based Treatment Simulator
value.description: Multiscale, multi-compartment agent-based model of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. assertion.description: Immune-agent interactions drive loss of modeled oligodendrocytes, which is used as the simulation's cellular proxy for myelin injury and relapse.
assertion.limitations: Demyelination is reduced to oligodendrocyte loss in a simulated 3-mm3 white-matter volume. The model does not resolve myelin ultrastructure, tract-specific conduction, remyelination, or axonal injury, and the oligodendrocyte-loss threshold is not an individualized imaging model.

readouts.name: Oligodendrocyte loss during simulated relapse
readouts.interpretation: Rapid loss of modeled oligodendrocytes is the disease-layer readout for a demyelinating event; treatment benefit appears as fewer such losses.

selected_evidence.snippet: In the CNS, activated helper T cells engage with resident microglia. Upon recognition of myelin antigens, the microglia are reactivated and produce specific cytokines (such as IL-1, IL-6, IL-12, TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL-2) and chemokines that activate Th1 and Th17 cells, leading to an inflammatory cascade and subsequent destruction of oligodendrocytes.

value.name: Lesion-Aware Personalized Whole-Brain Conduction-Delay Model
value.description: Direct successor to the Virtual Multiple Sclerosis Patient model. It retains each participant's 84-region DTI connectome and noisy Stuart-Landau dynamics but augments distance-derived edge delays based on a shared whole-brain velocity with an additive tract-specific term derived from the fraction of each tract intersecting the participant's FLAIR lesion mask. Simulation-based inference estimates the patient-specific strength of the lesion-to-delay relationship.
value.base_model: Virtual Multiple Sclerosis Patient whole-brain model (PMID:38974971)
value.model_software: Custom Stuart-Landau simulator with the SBI toolbox

variables.name: Tract lesion fraction
variables.description: Fraction of voxels in the tract between regions j and k that intersect the participant's FLAIR lesion mask.

variables.name: Lesion-to-delay weight
variables.description: Subject-level parameter controlling how strongly tract lesion fraction increases propagation delay.

variables.name: Edge-specific conduction delay
variables.description: Baseline distance-over-velocity delay plus the lesion-weighted delay term for a structural connection.

variables.name: Global coupling strength
variables.description: Scalar multiplying the participant's structural-connectivity matrix.

variables.name: Alpha peak amplitude
variables.description: Empirical or simulated alpha-spectrum peak used in model inversion.

value.notes: A curator search on 2026-08-20 identified no paper-specific code repository or executable model archive, and the clinical inputs are available only on request. Curator inspection found that the open VBI package contains generic Stuart-Landau and SBI components but not this paper's lesion-specific gamma-by-tract formulation, so it is not cited as the model artifact. The article is CC BY 4.0, which licenses the paper rather than an unreleased implementation. Synthetic parameter recovery had slope 0.8 and showed boundary bias. The clinical analysis reuses the small cross-sectional source cohort from the 2024 model; the gamma term was not a statistically significant EDSS predictor, and longitudinal validation is still needed.

assertion.description: The model maps the fraction of each white-matter tract occupied by a patient-specific lesion to an additional edge-specific conduction delay, then infers a subject-level lesion-effect parameter from MEG spectra.
assertion.limitations: FLAIR lesion fraction is an imaging proxy, not a direct measure of myelin thickness, axon diameter, or active inflammation. The model does not generate lesions or simulate immune attack, remyelination, axonal damage, or progression. One scalar gamma applies the same lesion-to-delay rule to all affected tracts, source reconstruction is vulnerable to volume conduction, and alternative mechanisms can alter alpha spectra. The same 18-patient/20-control source cohort as the 2024 study was used, without longitudinal or external validation.

readouts.name: Lesion-weighted tract conduction delay
readouts.interpretation: More lesion involvement adds a larger modeled delay on the affected tract; this is a personalized functional proxy rather than direct lesion-wise electrophysiology.

readouts.name: Alpha-spectrum peak amplitude as lesion-effect weight increases
readouts.interpretation: Lower simulated alpha peak amplitude with larger lesion-effect weight is the spectral feature used to invert the patient-specific parameter.

selected_evidence.snippet: In this work, we use large-scale brain models and Bayesian model inversion to estimate how myelin lesions translate to longer conduction delays across the damaged tracts.

value.name: Virtual Multiple Sclerosis Patient Whole-Brain Model
value.description: Subject-specific delayed whole-brain model that couples 84 noisy Stuart-Landau oscillators according to each participant's DTI-derived connectome. variables.description: Scalar multiplying each subject's structural-connectivity matrix.

variables.description: Subject-level homogeneous conduction-speed parameter inferred by simulation-based Bayesian inversion.

variables.description: Frequency of the median source-reconstructed MEG alpha-spectrum peak.

variables.name: Alpha peak amplitude
variables.description: Peak amplitude of the median 8-13-Hz power spectral density.

variables.name: Total alpha power
variables.description: Area under the median power spectral density from 8 to 13 Hz.

value.notes: Curator inspection on 2026-08-20 used repository commit 67cb165d2631f73cfae79643accf7bae3e7b4ef1 (also tagged v1.0). No LICENSE file or license grant was present; an MIT classifier in setup.py is not sufficient to license the code. The repository contains the delayed Stuart-Landau forward solver and an SBI demonstration, but not the clinical connectomes, MEG inputs, trained posterior, or complete 38-subject analysis. In the curator's smoke test, the default install failed to build the SWIG extension; after a manual build and dependency repairs, a synthetic three-node forward simulation produced finite time series and an alpha-band PSD. Curator comparison also found material paper/code differences in simulation duration, noise scale, priors, alpha band, and feature count. Reproducing the clinical findings therefore requires restricted data and missing workflow components. The paper reports a patent application and calls for larger multicenter replication.

assertion.description: The inverse model treats slower large-scale signal propagation as a functional consequence of myelin damage and infers an individual average conduction velocity from the participant's connectome and MEG spectrum.
assertion.limitations: The model does not simulate immune attack, myelin loss, lesion formation, remyelination, or axonal injury. It collapses spatially heterogeneous conduction into one homogeneous whole-brain velocity, and alpha-spectrum changes can also arise from excitation/inhibition balance, 1/f structure, or thalamic-loop changes. The evidence comes from 18 patients and 20 controls at one site; EDSS was available for 17 patients, and no external or longitudinal validation cohort was used.

readouts.name: Inferred average whole-brain conduction velocity
readouts.interpretation: A lower inferred velocity is interpreted as the aggregate functional effect of myelin damage, not a direct measurement of lesion-wise demyelination.

selected_evidence.snippet: In conclusion, we propose a principled way to link the most relevant physiopathological feature in MS, namely the slower conduction velocities across the brain network induced by myelin damage, to a large-scale observable quantity, that is the modification of the frequency spectrum.

assertion.name: Boolean Network Model of FA/BRCA Pathway
assertion.description: A Boolean network model incorporating the FA/BRCA DNA repair pathway, checkpoint proteins, and alternative DNA repair pathways. Simulates ICL repair, checkpoint activation, and predicts which alternative repair pathways become active when the FA/BRCA pathway is defective. The largest network model incorporating a DNA repair pathway at time of publication.

divergences.description: No cell-cycle timing and no lesion burden. Interstrand-crosslink repair is replication-coupled and its failure is dose-dependent, so both are material to how the deficiency manifests even though the pathway logic is reproduced.
The haematopoietic stem-cell context in which this repair deficiency becomes clinically manifest -- as marrow failure -- is not represented.

The network is parameter-free, with rules asserted from pathway literature rather than fitted. Recorded because it is a real property of the model, but immaterial to this link: the claim is that the FA/BRCA pathway logic reproduces crosslink repair, which is a structural claim rather than a quantitative one.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The network's core function is the FA/BRCA-mediated repair of DNA interstrand crosslinks; simulating loss-of-function mutants reproduces the repair failure that defines this node.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: A parameter-free Boolean abstraction of a single repair pathway in isolation: it has no cell-cycle timing, no lesion burden, and no representation of the haematopoietic context in which the repair deficiency becomes clinically manifest.

readouts.name: Simulated ICL repair under FA/BRCA-deficient genotypes
readouts.interpretation: Mutant simulations fail to complete the crosslink repair process that the wild-type network completes.

divergences.description: Homologous recombination appears as network components inside a crosslink-repair model, so what the model reports is the activation state of those components. The node describes recombination fidelity and outcome, which is a different quantity. This is the whole reason the link is PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES -- and note that model and target sit at the same biological scale, so no scale comparison would surface it.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Double-strand-break repair is among the processes the network simulates, and the alternative-pathway predictions concern which repair routes compensate when the FA/BRCA arm is lost.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Homologous recombination is represented as network components within a crosslink-repair model rather than modelled as a resolution mechanism in its own right, so the model speaks to pathway activation state rather than to recombination fidelity or outcome.

findings.statement: The model simulates ICL repair mediated by the FA/BRCA pathway
Alternative DNA repair pathways are predicted to become active when FA/BRCA is defective
Checkpoint protein activation patterns emerge from recurrent DNA damage
Mutant simulations generated predictions about FA/BRCA pathway function that had not been reported experimentally.

assertion.name: DNA Methylation Episignature Classifier
assertion.description: Machine learning classifier trained on genome-wide DNA methylation profiles from peripheral blood of FA patients. assertion.name: M4RL Glioblastoma Tumor-Microenvironment Treatment Model
assertion.description: Multiscale framework combining a spatial agent-based model of tumor cells, tumor-associated macrophages, cytokines, and intracellular ERK/AKT signaling with a Fokker-Planck physics-informed neural-network surrogate and A3C reinforcement learning to optimize CSF1R- and IGF1R-inhibitor scheduling.
assertion.model_software: C++ multiscale agent-based model; Python/PyTorch PINN and A3C
assertion.model_format: C++/Python/CSV/PyTorch checkpoint (.pth)

modeled_mechanisms.description: The agent-based model explicitly represents M0, M1, and M2 macrophage states and perturbs their polarization through simulated CSF1R inhibition.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The discrete M0/M1/M2 states simplify a continuous macrophage phenotype spectrum, and the treatment response was evaluated computationally and against preclinical rather than prospective patient data.

readouts.name: M2-to-M1 macrophage repolarization under CSF1R inhibition
readouts.interpretation: The simulated shift toward M1 macrophages is a direct readout of the model's macrophage-polarization mechanism, not evidence of clinical repolarization in patients.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The model perturbs tumor-cell proliferation indirectly through simulated CSF1R inhibition of macrophage polarization and IGF1R inhibition of tumor cells, using tumor-cell density and predicted survival as optimization outputs.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Validation is preclinical and computational rather than prospective or patient-specific, and the modeled glioblastoma is not stratified by IDH status. The agent model reduces macrophages to M0/M1/M2 states, omits T cells and other signaling pathways, and represents vasculature only as a source of recruited macrophages and drug penetration.

readouts.name: Tumor-cell density under optimized combination treatment
readouts.interpretation: Lower simulated tumor-cell density reports suppression of the modeled proliferative endpoint under the optimized schedule; it does not establish efficacy in people with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

assertion.name: Yoon multivariate DMD progression and virtual-trial models
assertion.description: Five nonlinear mixed-effects progression models derived from the prospective longitudinal ImagingNMD cohort. Each model couples six-minute walk distance to MRI transverse relaxation time in one leg muscle and simulates how age, steroid use, baseline function, and baseline imaging alter virtual-patient trajectories.
assertion.model_format: Nonlinear mixed-effects sigmoid Imax and Emax models

modeled_mechanisms.description: Uses age-dependent decline in walking distance and rise in muscle MRI-T2 to estimate heterogeneous human DMD progression trajectories.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: This is a cohort-derived statistical virtual-patient model rather than a mechanistic tissue twin. It was developed in individuals ambulatory at baseline, excludes disease-modifying treatment effects, and does not represent the early developmental gain in walking ability before age five.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Treats longitudinal muscle MRI-T2 as a quantitative imaging readout associated with replacement of contractile muscle by noncontractile tissue.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: MRI-T2 is not specific to fat or fibrosis and can also reflect edema and inflammation; muscle-specific trajectories cannot be generalized to every skeletal muscle or to cardiac tissue.

variables.description: MRI-T2 for one of five modeled leg muscles

variables.description: Time metric for the disease-progression trajectories

variables.description: Covariate indicating corticosteroid treatment status

variables.description: Age at which six-minute walk distance reaches half its maximum decrease

variables.description: Age at which muscle MRI-T2 reaches half its maximum increase

findings.statement: Sigmoid Imax and Emax functions best captured functional decline and MRI-T2 increase, with steroid use and baseline functional and imaging values as significant covariates.
The five models produced similar half-decline ages for walking distance but muscle-specific half-increase ages for MRI-T2.

assertion.notes: The public simulator supports real and virtual populations for trial-design use. The DIGITAL_TWIN label denotes individualized covariate-conditioned trajectories, not a mechanistic or continuously updated personal twin; clinical use beyond trial simulation would require external validation in the intended population.

selected_evidence.snippet: Disease progression models were developed by a nonlinear mixed-effect modeling approach. Univariate models of 6MWD and MRI-T2 of five muscles were developed separately. Age at assessment was the time metric. Multivariate models were developed by estimating the correlation of 6MWD and MRI-T2 model variables.

assertion.name: Virgilio agent-based model of regeneration in healthy and mdx skeletal muscle
assertion.description: Spatial stochastic model of an acutely injured mouse muscle cross-section in which muscle fibers, extracellular matrix, necrotic tissue, fibroblasts, satellite stem cells, myogenic progenitors, neutrophils, and macrophage states interact over 28 days. Disease scenarios alter microenvironmental cell behaviors and initial injury using age-specific mdx experimental observations.
assertion.model_format: Java agent-based simulation with histology-derived two-dimensional geometry

modeled_mechanisms.description: Simulates satellite-cell activation, proliferation, differentiation, and their contribution to recovery of injured muscle cross-sectional area.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model represents acute injury in young and aged mdx mouse muscle, not chronic human DMD progression; mdx disease is substantially milder than the human disorder, and cross-sectional area is not a direct measure of strength.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Represents neutrophils and multiple pro- and anti-inflammatory macrophage states as regulators of regeneration after contraction-induced injury.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Immune behavior is encoded as literature-derived rules in a two-dimensional acute-injury setting and omits systemic immunity and the chronic inflammatory history of human DMD muscle.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Tracks fibroblast and extracellular-matrix behavior as microenvironmental determinants of regeneration in mdx scenarios.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model does not reproduce long-term fatty replacement and only represents a small muscle cross-section over 28 days.

findings.statement: Recovery at day 28 depended on peak satellite stem-cell abundance, with suppressed peaks emerging in the impaired-regeneration aged-mdx scenario.
Fibroblast and anti-inflammatory macrophage populations influenced satellite stem-cell abundance, but no single altered parameter explained the disease difference.

assertion.notes: No durable public deposit of the exact 2018 Repast implementation was identified. This is an mdx mouse model, not a human or patient-specific DMD digital twin; its value is hypothesis generation about regeneration microenvironments.

selected_evidence.snippet: The goals of this project were to 1) develop an agent-based model of skeletal muscle that predicts the dynamic regenerative response of muscle cells, fibroblasts, SSCs, and inflammatory cells as a result of contraction-induced injury, 2) calibrate and validate the model parameters based on comparisons with published experimental measurements, and 3) use the model to investigate how changing isolated and combined factors known to be associated with DMD (e.g., altered fibroblast or SSC behaviors) influence muscle regeneration.

assertion.name: Virgilio fibrosis-perturbation model of mdx muscle regeneration
assertion.description: Follow-up use of the skeletal-muscle agent-based framework to vary extracellular-matrix area fraction and protein density, predict their effects on cell migration, growth-factor diffusion, and 28-day regeneration, and compare the prediction with TGF-beta-treated mdx mouse experiments.
assertion.base_model: Virgilio-mdx-muscle-regeneration-2018
assertion.model_format: Java agent-based simulation with two-dimensional muscle geometry

modeled_mechanisms.description: Independently varies extracellular-matrix occupied area and effective protein density to test how distinct fibrosis properties affect regeneration.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Fibrosis is represented by area fraction and density in mdx mouse muscle; matrix composition, architecture, fatty infiltration, and years-long human disease evolution are not represented.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Predicts regeneration loss through restricted cell migration and growth-factor diffusion, then revises that prediction when matrix density is reduced.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Regeneration is assessed using cross-sectional area 28 days after an acute injury, not human muscle function or longitudinal DMD progression.

variables.name: Extracellular matrix area fraction
variables.description: Fraction of the simulated cross-section occupied by extracellular matrix

variables.name: Extracellular matrix protein density
variables.description: Effective matrix density controlling stiffness and transport constraints

variables.name: Growth-factor diffusion
variables.description: Effective diffusion of regenerative signals through extracellular matrix

variables.name: Cell migration
variables.description: Effective movement of regenerative cells through the matrix

variables.name: Muscle cross-sectional area recovery
variables.description: Regenerated muscle area at 28 days after injury

findings.statement: Increasing simulated fibrotic area initially reduced day-28 regeneration by limiting growth-factor diffusion and cell migration.

The TGF-beta experiment did not show the predicted recovery difference; additional simulations reproduced that negative result when matrix protein density was reduced, showing that area fraction alone was insufficient.

assertion.notes: This follow-up is especially useful as a negative-result case: the first model prediction failed when fibrosis area increased but matrix density fell. It should not be generalized from mdx mice to antifibrotic efficacy in people with DMD.

selected_evidence.snippet: This study (1) used an agent-based model to predict the effect of increased fibrosis in mdx muscle on regeneration from injury, and (2) experimentally tested the resulting model-derived hypothesis.

assertion.name: UVA/Padova Type 1 Diabetes Simulator
assertion.description: Simulator of glucose-insulin dynamics with a population of in silico subjects with type 1 diabetes, built on the Dalla Man meal model of the glucose-insulin system. The 2013 version (S2013) adds nonlinear insulin-dependent glucose utilization in hypoglycemia and glucagon kinetics, secretion and action. It is used for in silico trials of glucose sensors, insulin dosing and closed-loop (artificial pancreas) controllers, and its developers report that FDA accepted it in 2008 as a substitute for animal trials in pre-clinical testing of insulin treatment strategies; no FDA document recording that decision is cited here. It describes the type 1 diabetes subtype only, not the other forms this umbrella entry covers.
assertion.base_model: Dalla Man meal simulation model of the glucose-insulin system (PMID:17926672)

modeled_mechanisms.description: Simulates plasma glucose excursions after meals and insulin doses in virtual type 1 diabetes subjects, the glycemic state at the head of this node. The complication cascade the node goes on to describe is not modelled.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The virtual subjects have absent endogenous insulin secretion by construction; autoimmune beta-cell destruction, residual beta-cell function and diabetic complications are not modelled. It applies only to the type 1 diabetes subtype of this entry, and its glucose output is short-term dynamics rather than chronic hyperglycemia over years.

divergences.description: Loss of insulin secretion is an input to the simulator, not an outcome of modelled autoimmunity; this does not affect its use for simulating glucose responses to insulin therapy.

The node continues from sustained hyperglycemia into oxidative and AGE-RAGE stress, endothelial injury and end-organ complications; none of these is in the simulator, which stops at plasma glucose and insulin.
The node's hyperglycemia is sustained over years; the underlying meal model describes single meals and a day of meals, so the simulator describes glucose control rather than chronic exposure.
The node spans every diabetes subtype in this entry, while the virtual population is calibrated to type 1 diabetes only, so the link does not extend to type 2, monogenic or gestational diabetes.

findings.statement: The simulator's developers report that FDA accepted it in January 2008 as a substitute for animal trials in pre-clinical testing of insulin treatment strategies.

assertion.name: Subcellular sodium-channel myocardial strand model
assertion.description: A one-dimensional strand of 300 human epicardial ventricular myocytes for studying how subcellular sodium-channel distribution changes action-potential morphology and propagation. Each cell is divided into lateral and pre- and post-junctional membrane segments, represented by a modified O'Hara-Rudy dynamic model with ten Tusscher-Panfilov fast sodium current and an experimentally based rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current. Cells are coupled through gap junctions and ephaptic interactions. The disease-like manipulation reduces lateral-membrane sodium conductance while retaining junctional sodium conductance.
assertion.base_model: Modified O'Hara-Rudy dynamic 2011 human ventricular model with ten Tusscher-Panfilov fast INa and experimental IKr
assertion.model_software: C/Autotools; Intel C Compiler, Intel MKL/PARDISO, and Intel OpenMP (original configuration)
assertion.model_format: C source, Autotools build files, and positional text input

variables.name: Lateral-membrane sodium conductance fraction
variables.description: Fast and late lateral-membrane sodium conductance expressed as a percentage of control.

variables.name: Action-potential membrane voltage
variables.description: Membrane-potential trajectory for each modeled cell and membrane segment.

variables.name: Conduction velocity
variables.description: Propagation velocity along the myocardial strand in centimeters per second, derived in the publication from activation-time outputs rather than emitted directly by the code.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The model directly reduces lateral-membrane sodium conductance and measures the resulting action-potential changes, rather than reproducing the full genetically and structurally heterogeneous Brugada mechanism.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Sodium-channel reduction is prescribed phenomenologically rather than generated by an SCN5A allele, trafficking defect, or patient-calibrated expression state. The model does not represent broader calcium- or potassium-channel causes of reduced depolarization reserve.

readouts.name: Action-potential dome morphology
readouts.description: Progressive lateral sodium-channel reduction produces notch-and-dome, delayed-dome, and loss-of-dome action potentials.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reduced lateral sodium conductance lowers modeled upstroke velocity and strand conduction velocity, recapitulating the conduction-slowing component of the Brugada substrate.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: This is a homogeneous one-dimensional generic epicardial ventricular strand, not an anatomically reconstructed RVOT. It omits patient-specific geometry, fibrosis, fiber organization, ECG leads, and clinical conduction maps.

readouts.name: Conduction velocity
readouts.description: Conduction velocity falls as lateral-membrane sodium conductance is reduced from control to complete loss.

findings.statement: In the homogeneous-conductance comparison, reducing lateral-membrane sodium conductance from 100% to 0% lowers conduction velocity from 71.4 to 25.0 cm/s.

assertion.notes: The repository is pinned at commit 90962d4c159d5b12133d99cb0818c84c6746a013 and has no release, CI, container, or dependency lock. COPYING declares GPL-3.0, but src/pardiso_mat.c carries an Intel Confidential notice that restricts use, copying, and distribution; the effective reuse and redistribution status is therefore ambiguous. The checked-in build targets legacy Intel C Compiler, MKL/PARDISO, and OpenMP paths and flags. It did not compile unmodified during curator testing on ARM macOS. The fixed-step explicit-Euler simulation uses a 1-microsecond step for 30 beats. Its only sample input is stale: for the supplied one-dataset, 43-state configuration, the parser reads 83 numeric fields whereas check_test/in supplies 82, shifting later values and preventing a faithful run. No paper-scenario manifest, expected outputs, or automated tests are supplied. The code emits voltage and ionic traces plus activation times but does not directly calculate CV; nai_data.out and ki_data.out are also mislabeled relative to their written state indices. The article is CC BY 4.0. The model was compared qualitatively with prior mouse and human electrophysiology, but it was not fitted to or independently validated in a Brugada patient cohort.

selected_evidence.snippet: We constructed in silico human ventricular myocardial strand and ring models, and examined whether the Na+ channel expression changes in each myocyte cause the phase-2 reentry in BrS.

assertion.name: Spatially heterogeneous sodium-channel myocardial ring model
assertion.description: A one-dimensional ring of 600 human epicardial ventricular myocytes using the same modified O'Hara-Rudy ionic model, segmented cell membranes, gap junctions, and ephaptic coupling as the companion strand model. Two ring regions are assigned different, markedly reduced lateral-membrane sodium conductances to test whether spatial heterogeneity converts phase-2 reentry into intermittent or persistent circulating reentrant excitation.
assertion.base_model: Modified O'Hara-Rudy dynamic 2011 human ventricular model with ten Tusscher-Panfilov fast INa and experimental IKr
assertion.model_software: C/Autotools; Intel C Compiler, Intel MKL/PARDISO, and Intel OpenMP (original configuration)
assertion.model_format: C source, Autotools build files, and positional text input

variables.name: Regional lateral-membrane sodium conductance fractions
variables.description: Separately imposed percentages of control lateral sodium conductance in the two ring regions.

variables.name: Action-potential propagation pattern
variables.description: Spatiotemporal membrane-voltage propagation around the ring; block, phase-2 reentry, and circulating reentry are interpreted from the traces rather than classified directly by the code.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The heterogeneous ring produces phase-2-reentry-mediated circulating excitation, representing a reduced tissue-scale mechanism for Brugada reentrant tachyarrhythmia.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The 600-cell one-dimensional ring is not an RVOT or whole-heart geometry and cannot reproduce polymorphic VT, ventricular fibrillation, surface ECG, hemodynamics, or patient outcomes. Reentry depends on imposed and locally extreme sodium-conductance heterogeneity rather than measured patient tissue or a disease genotype.

readouts.name: Phase-2-reentry-mediated reentrant arrhythmia
readouts.description: Spatially heterogeneous lateral sodium-channel reduction produces intermittent or persistent unidirectional circulating excitation.

findings.statement: Reentry occurred mainly when region B lateral sodium conductance was below 5% of control and region A was between 5% and 10%, underscoring dependence on an extreme imposed spatial gradient.

assertion.notes: The repository is pinned at commit 0a6aece22925ca48430d775589547bbfbf9e0ff0 and has no release, CI, container, dependency lock, or sample input. The checked-in build targets legacy Intel C Compiler, MKL/PARDISO, and OpenMP paths and flags and did not compile unmodified during curator testing on ARM macOS. The fixed-step explicit-Euler simulation uses a 1-microsecond step for 30 beats, nominally 30 million steps. The article is CC BY 4.0. This is a hypothesis-driven mechanism model, not an allele-specific, anatomically personalized, or clinically predictive ventricular simulation.

value.name: Type 1 Interferon Signalling Boolean Model
value.description: An executable, dynamic Boolean model of type 1 interferon signalling derived from the COVID-19 Disease Map interferon diagram using CaSQ and the same map-to-model framework as the rheumatoid arthritis FLS model. Simulated in Cell Collective under virus infection, inflammatory conditions, and both combined, it yields 128 stable states and no oscillations, which are clustered by four output nodes — viral replication, antiviral response, inflammation, and IFNA1 secretion. Systematic single-node knockouts across this and companion apoptosis and macrophage models were used to nominate drug targets.
value.notes: Curated as part of the Boolean/logical modelling track; see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-28-boolean-modeling-and-pathographs.md. Two companion Boolean models from the same work — respiratory epithelium apoptosis and macrophage immune-cell recruitment — were embedded in a multiscale lung-infection simulator; they are not separately curated here. Literature-referenced, not runnable in-repo.

assertion.name: Skin Allergy Risk Assessment (SARA) model
assertion.description: A Bayesian model that infers a human-relevant sensitizer potency metric and a risk measure for a given consumer exposure from any combination of human patch test, local lymph node assay, DPRA, KeratinoSens, h-CLAT or U-SENS data.

variables.name: Human repeat insult patch test result
variables.description: Human in vivo reference input. The model takes any combination of its six input types rather than a fixed set.

variables.name: Local lymph node assay result
variables.description: Murine in vivo reference input, curated in this entry as its own animal model.

variables.name: Direct peptide reactivity assay result
variables.description: Peptide reactivity input.

variables.name: KeratinoSens result
variables.description: Keratinocyte reporter input.

variables.name: Human cell line activation test result
variables.description: Dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, curated in this entry as its own experimental model, which records CD86 and CD54 as the measured quantity.

variables.name: U-SENS result
variables.description: A second dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, measured in the U937 line.

variables.name: Sensitiser potency metric
variables.description: The model's inferred human-relevant potency estimate, carrying explicit quantification of uncertainty. Neither source states the unit, so none is recorded here.

variables.name: Margin of exposure
variables.description: The ratio of the potency estimate to the consumer exposure level, which is the quantity regressed against the clinical benchmark classifications.

variables.name: Probability that an exposure is low risk
variables.description: The risk metric the model reports for a given consumer exposure. Deriving it by regression against benchmark risk classifications is what lets the model avoid applying safety assessment factors to a non-animal point of departure.

assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link, because what it predicts is the sensitization outcome and this entry has no adverse-outcome node to attach that to; see the no_node_for_integrated_outcome_prediction discussion. The potency metric is inferred statistically rather than measured, and the model is anchored on human patch test and local lymph node assay reference data, so it inherits those reference sets' domains. Whether the safety assessment factors used with animal data suit a non-animal point of departure is unresolved.

selected_evidence.snippet: It is currently unclear whether these safety assessment factors are appropriate when using non-animal test data to derive a point-of departure.

assertion.name: Decision-tree defined approach with Derek Nexus and a k-nearest-neighbours potency model
assertion.description: A defined approach that applies exclusion criteria to prioritise in chemico and in vitro sources covering key events 1 to 3, combines them in a two out of three hazard call, and assigns a potency category using a k-nearest-neighbours model built on human and local lymph node assay data.
assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link for the same reason as the SARA model: it integrates the per-key-event assay readouts into a hazard and potency prediction for the outcome, and this entry has no adverse-outcome node. Its inputs cover key events 1 to 3, so no single node corresponds to it either. Hazard accuracy is about 85 to 86 percent against local lymph node assay and human reference data, but the correct potency category is reached for only 59 to 68 percent of chemicals. The structural component rests on chemical structure and statistical association rather than on the molecular processes of sensitization.

selected_evidence.snippet: Although NAMs have achieved substantial regulatory maturity for this endpoint, most computational approaches-including structural alerts, read-across, and quantitative structure-activity relationship models-rely predominantly on chemical structure and statistical associations, with limited representation of the molecular processes underlying sensitization.

assertion.name: Skin Allergy Risk Assessment - Integrated Chemical Environment (SARA-ICE)
assertion.description: A Bayesian framework for quantitative skin sensitization hazard and potency assessment, developed by NICEATM and Unilever, that estimates the ED01: the dermal dose associated with a 1 percent sensitization probability in humans. It integrates in chemico and in vitro assay results and can also take historical human and murine data. Two implementations share the one model. SARA-ICE DA is a fixed defined approach accepted into OECD Guideline 497 for deriving a point of departure and usable under Mutual Acceptance of Data; it reports the point of departure as the geometric mean of the ED01 distribution. SARA-ICE Extended returns the full ED01 distribution, a prediction uncertainty ratio, and probabilities for the GHS subcategories.

variables.name: Direct peptide reactivity assay result
variables.description: Peptide reactivity input. The curated SARA-ICE training database holds 650 direct peptide reactivity assay results.

variables.name: Kinetic direct peptide reactivity assay result
variables.description: Rate-based peptide reactivity input, and the one input class the earlier SARA model did not take. The training database holds 361 results.

variables.name: KeratinoSens result
variables.description: Keratinocyte reporter input. The training database holds 972 results, the largest of the non-animal input sets.

variables.name: Human cell line activation test result
variables.description: Dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, curated in this entry as its own experimental model. The training database holds 431 results.

variables.name: U937 cell line activation test result
variables.description: A second dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, measured in the U937 line. The training database holds 164 results, the smallest input set.

variables.name: Human predictive patch test result
variables.description: Human in vivo reference input, comprising human maximization test and human repeat-insult patch test data. The training database holds 871 results, 506 maximization and 365 repeat-insult.

variables.name: Local lymph node assay result
variables.description: Murine in vivo reference input, curated in this entry as its own animal model. The training database holds 536 results.

variables.name: ED01
variables.description: The model's estimated quantity: the dermal dose associated with a 1 percent sensitization probability in a theoretical human predictive patch test population. Reported as a distribution whose variance measures the uncertainty in the estimate, summarised as the interval between the 5th and 95th percentiles.

variables.name: SARA-ICE DA point of departure
variables.description: The point of departure the fixed defined approach reports, calculated as the geometric mean of the ED01 distribution on the assumption that the chemical is a sensitizer. The distribution is bounded above at 60000 ug/cm2, the GHS Category 1 boundary.

variables.name: SARA-ICE prediction uncertainty ratio
variables.description: The Extended implementation's summary measure of estimate uncertainty, the ratio between the 5th and 50th percentiles of the ED01 distribution.

variables.name: GHS subcategory probability
variables.description: The Extended implementation's probability of assignment to GHS Subcategory 1A, Subcategory 1B, or Not Categorized, taken as the probability mass either side of the 500 and 60000 ug/cm2 thresholds.

assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link for the same reason as the SARA model above: it predicts the sensitization outcome from inputs spanning several key events, and this entry has no adverse-outcome node to attach that to; see the no_node_for_integrated_outcome_prediction discussion. A separate record from the SARA model rather than a re-curation of it, because SARA-ICE was built on the Unilever SARA model with an expanded training set drawn from the NICEATM Integrated Chemical Environment database and a curated human predictive patch test set, names the ED01 as its output quantity, and takes kinetic direct peptide reactivity assay results, which SARA does not. The two implementations are recorded as one model because the source presents them as two implementations of one Bayesian framework, differing in output and in whether a user can change them: the defined approach is fixed and cannot be altered outside a guideline update, while Extended is versioned and may gain input types. The human input is the same quantity the SARA record calls human repeat insult patch test; the later paper uses the umbrella term human predictive patch test for the maximization and repeat-insult tests together. The defined approach requires at least two key event inputs to be acceptable under Mutual Acceptance of Data. Two limits on what the evaluation supports. Specificity for non-sensitizers was lower than sensitivity, so the model is more reliable at identifying a sensitizer than at clearing a non-sensitizer; and GHS subcategorization accuracy of 33 to 77 percent means the potency category is considerably weaker than the hazard call, as it is for the defined approach recorded above. The input enumeration and every per-assay count in this record come from the source's Methods section 2.1.1, which describes a database of 434 distinct chemicals and nearly 5000 data points; that section is not in the cached abstract, so no snippet here covers those figures. Two further statements in this record are beyond the cached abstract in the same way, and no snippet covers them either: the abstract records acceptance by the OECD and use under Mutual Acceptance of Data without naming Guideline 497, which the source identifies in its introduction, and the defined approach's two-key-event input requirement, which is in Methods section 2.1.2. The 180 substances in the evidence below are the evaluation set, tested in the direct peptide reactivity assay, KeratinoSens and the human cell line activation test only, and are not the training database. What this source does not give is each input's measured endpoint and unit as the model consumes it: it states the assay names and defers the model's internals to Reinke et al. 2025 and Reynolds et al. 2019 and 2022. The endpoints are therefore recorded here only where this entry already curates the assay as its own model.

selected_evidence.snippet: For GHS subcategorization, accuracy ranged from 33-77% with low underprediction (8-21%), with concordance highest with the Guideline 497 DAs
