assertion.name: Skin Sensitization Prediction Model (SSPM)
assertion.description: An algorithm that compares a proposed cosmetic or personal-care formulation against a database of more than 20 years of human repeat insult patch test (HRIPT) results on 1274 product formulations and 1226 common ingredients, tested on 203,640 human subjects, to set per-ingredient and per-formulation risk thresholds from dosage density, occlusion potential, skin-barrier-impairment potential, and potential effects on immune-primed skin.
assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link for the same reason as the SARA model: it predicts a formulation-level sensitization risk call rather than measuring any single mechanism step, and this entry has no adverse-outcome node to attach that to; see the no_node_for_integrated_outcome_prediction discussion. It is a rule-based risk-threshold calculator over historical human test data rather than a trained statistical or machine-learning model, so no ComputationalModelTypeEnum value is a good fit and model_type is left unset. Its reference data is a separate, proprietary HRIPT database rather than the published HPPT database (PMID:37615678, in this entry's references catalog) that the other assay-validation records cite.

selected_evidence.snippet: The SSPM sets modifiable thresholds for each individual ingredient of a proposed formulation and for the formulation as a whole, applying risk calculations based on dosage density, potential for skin occlusion, potential for skin barrier impairment, and potential effects on immune-primed skin.

assertion.name: Skin Allergy Risk Assessment (SARA) model
assertion.description: A Bayesian model that infers a human-relevant sensitizer potency metric and a risk measure for a given consumer exposure from any combination of human patch test, local lymph node assay, DPRA, KeratinoSens, h-CLAT or U-SENS data.

variables.name: Human repeat insult patch test result
variables.description: Human in vivo reference input. The model takes any combination of its six input types rather than a fixed set.

variables.name: Local lymph node assay result
variables.description: Murine in vivo reference input, curated in this entry as its own animal model.

variables.name: Direct peptide reactivity assay result
variables.description: Peptide reactivity input.

variables.name: KeratinoSens result
variables.description: Keratinocyte reporter input.

variables.name: Human cell line activation test result
variables.description: Dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, curated in this entry as its own experimental model, which records CD86 and CD54 as the measured quantity.

variables.name: U-SENS result
variables.description: A second dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, measured in the U937 line.

variables.name: Sensitiser potency metric
variables.description: The model's inferred human-relevant potency estimate, carrying explicit quantification of uncertainty. Neither source states the unit, so none is recorded here.

variables.name: Margin of exposure
variables.description: The ratio of the potency estimate to the consumer exposure level, which is the quantity regressed against the clinical benchmark classifications.

variables.name: Probability that an exposure is low risk
variables.description: The risk metric the model reports for a given consumer exposure. Deriving it by regression against benchmark risk classifications is what lets the model avoid applying safety assessment factors to a non-animal point of departure.

assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link, because what it predicts is the sensitization outcome and this entry has no adverse-outcome node to attach that to; see the no_node_for_integrated_outcome_prediction discussion. The potency metric is inferred statistically rather than measured, and the model is anchored on human patch test and local lymph node assay reference data, so it inherits those reference sets' domains. Whether the safety assessment factors used with animal data suit a non-animal point of departure is unresolved.

selected_evidence.snippet: Margins-of-exposure (potency estimate to consumer exposure level ratio) are regressed against the benchmark risk classifications, enabling derivation of a risk metric defined as the probability that an exposure is low risk.

assertion.name: Skin Allergy Risk Assessment - Integrated Chemical Environment (SARA-ICE)
assertion.description: A Bayesian framework for quantitative skin sensitization hazard and potency assessment, developed by NICEATM and Unilever, that estimates the ED01: the dermal dose associated with a 1 percent sensitization probability in humans. It integrates in chemico and in vitro assay results and can also take historical human and murine data. Two implementations share the one model. SARA-ICE DA is a fixed defined approach accepted into OECD Guideline 497 for deriving a point of departure and usable under Mutual Acceptance of Data; it reports the point of departure as the geometric mean of the ED01 distribution. SARA-ICE Extended returns the full ED01 distribution, a prediction uncertainty ratio, and probabilities for the GHS subcategories.

variables.name: Direct peptide reactivity assay result
variables.description: Peptide reactivity input. The curated SARA-ICE training database holds 650 direct peptide reactivity assay results.

variables.name: Kinetic direct peptide reactivity assay result
variables.description: Rate-based peptide reactivity input, and the one input class the earlier SARA model did not take. The training database holds 361 results.

variables.name: KeratinoSens result
variables.description: Keratinocyte reporter input. The training database holds 972 results, the largest of the non-animal input sets.

variables.name: Human cell line activation test result
variables.description: Dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, curated in this entry as its own experimental model. The training database holds 431 results.

variables.name: U937 cell line activation test result
variables.description: A second dendritic-cell-surrogate activation input, measured in the U937 line. The training database holds 164 results, the smallest input set.

variables.name: Human predictive patch test result
variables.description: Human in vivo reference input, comprising human maximization test and human repeat-insult patch test data. The training database holds 871 results, 506 maximization and 365 repeat-insult.

variables.name: Local lymph node assay result
variables.description: Murine in vivo reference input, curated in this entry as its own animal model. The training database holds 536 results.

variables.name: ED01
variables.description: The model's estimated quantity: the dermal dose associated with a 1 percent sensitization probability in a theoretical human predictive patch test population. Reported as a distribution whose variance measures the uncertainty in the estimate, summarised as the interval between the 5th and 95th percentiles.

variables.name: SARA-ICE DA point of departure
variables.description: The point of departure the fixed defined approach reports, calculated as the geometric mean of the ED01 distribution on the assumption that the chemical is a sensitizer. The distribution is bounded above at 60000 ug/cm2, the GHS Category 1 boundary.

variables.name: SARA-ICE prediction uncertainty ratio
variables.description: The Extended implementation's summary measure of estimate uncertainty, the ratio between the 5th and 50th percentiles of the ED01 distribution.

variables.name: GHS subcategory probability
variables.description: The Extended implementation's probability of assignment to GHS Subcategory 1A, Subcategory 1B, or Not Categorized, taken as the probability mass either side of the 500 and 60000 ug/cm2 thresholds.

assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link for the same reason as the SARA model above: it predicts the sensitization outcome from inputs spanning several key events, and this entry has no adverse-outcome node to attach that to; see the no_node_for_integrated_outcome_prediction discussion. A separate record from the SARA model rather than a re-curation of it, because SARA-ICE was built on the Unilever SARA model with an expanded training set drawn from the NICEATM Integrated Chemical Environment database and a curated human predictive patch test set, names the ED01 as its output quantity, and takes kinetic direct peptide reactivity assay results, which SARA does not. The two implementations are recorded as one model because the source presents them as two implementations of one Bayesian framework, differing in output and in whether a user can change them: the defined approach is fixed and cannot be altered outside a guideline update, while Extended is versioned and may gain input types. The human input is the same quantity the SARA record calls human repeat insult patch test; the later paper uses the umbrella term human predictive patch test for the maximization and repeat-insult tests together. The defined approach requires at least two key event inputs to be acceptable under Mutual Acceptance of Data. Two limits on what the evaluation supports. Specificity for non-sensitizers was lower than sensitivity, so the model is more reliable at identifying a sensitizer than at clearing a non-sensitizer; and GHS subcategorization accuracy of 33 to 77 percent means the potency category is considerably weaker than the hazard call, as it is for the defined approach recorded above. The input enumeration and every per-assay count in this record come from the source's Methods section 2.1.1, which describes a database of 434 distinct chemicals and nearly 5000 data points; that section is not in the cached abstract, so no snippet here covers those figures. Two further statements in this record are beyond the cached abstract in the same way, and no snippet covers them either: the abstract records acceptance by the OECD and use under Mutual Acceptance of Data without naming Guideline 497, which the source identifies in its introduction, and the defined approach's two-key-event input requirement, which is in Methods section 2.1.2. The 180 substances in the evidence below are the evaluation set, tested in the direct peptide reactivity assay, KeratinoSens and the human cell line activation test only, and are not the training database. What this source does not give is each input's measured endpoint and unit as the model consumes it: it states the assay names and defers the model's internals to Reinke et al. 2025 and Reynolds et al. 2019 and 2022. The endpoints are therefore recorded here only where this entry already curates the assay as its own model.

selected_evidence.snippet: SARA-ICE Extended, which returns ED01 distributions, a prediction uncertainty ratio, and probabilities for assignments to Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labeling of Chemicals (GHS) categories.

assertion.name: Skin Sensitization Prediction Model (SSPM)
assertion.description: An algorithm that compares a proposed cosmetic or personal-care formulation against a database of more than 20 years of human repeat insult patch test (HRIPT) results on 1274 product formulations and 1226 common ingredients, tested on 203,640 human subjects, to set per-ingredient and per-formulation risk thresholds from dosage density, occlusion potential, skin-barrier-impairment potential, and potential effects on immune-primed skin.
assertion.notes: Carries no mechanism link for the same reason as the SARA model: it predicts a formulation-level sensitization risk call rather than measuring any single mechanism step, and this entry has no adverse-outcome node to attach that to; see the no_node_for_integrated_outcome_prediction discussion. It is a rule-based risk-threshold calculator over historical human test data rather than a trained statistical or machine-learning model, so no ComputationalModelTypeEnum value is a good fit and model_type is left unset. Its reference data is a separate, proprietary HRIPT database rather than the published HPPT database (PMID:37615678, in this entry's references catalog) that the other assay-validation records cite.

selected_evidence.snippet: The novel Skin Sensitization Prediction Model (SSPM) is a methodology that draws upon a database consisting of more than 20 years of historical HRIPT data pertaining to 1274 unique product formulations, comprising 1226 common ingredients, for which HRIPT testing has been performed on 203,640 human subjects.

assertion.name: Virtual Epilepsy Patient Cohort brain twins
assertion.description: A cohort of 30 patient-specific whole-brain network models for drug-resistant epilepsy. Each twin combines T1 and diffusion MRI, reconstructed SEEG electrodes, structural connectivity, a regional Epileptor neural-mass model, and a patient-specific epileptogenic-zone hypothesis to generate spontaneous, stimulation-induced, and interictal brain activity.
assertion.model_software: Python; The Virtual Brain; Epileptor; MNE-Python; NumPy; SciPy
assertion.model_format: Python scripts with an external iEEG-BIDS virtual-patient dataset

modeled_mechanisms.description: Patient-specific regional excitability and structural coupling generate synthetic seizure-onset and propagation patterns that can be projected to each patient's reconstructed SEEG electrodes.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Validation is retrospective and feature-level rather than a prospective demonstration that the model improves treatment decisions. SEEG only samples implanted regions, the Epileptor is a reduced neural-mass model, and the virtual cohort uses inferred epileptogenic-zone parameters as its synthetic ground truth.

readouts.name: Spatiotemporal spontaneous-seizure similarity
readouts.interpretation: Correlation, channel overlap, and seizure-onset/propagation similarity compare each synthetic SEEG seizure with its empirical counterpart.

readouts.name: Interictal spike-count distribution
readouts.interpretation: The fraction of detected spikes at each SEEG electrode tests whether the model reproduces the patient's spatial distribution of interictal activity.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Bayesian inversion of spontaneous SEEG assigns each brain region an excitability parameter that determines whether it can autonomously generate seizures or is recruited through structural coupling.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Regional excitability is a latent model parameter, not a direct cellular electrophysiology measurement, and different cellular mechanisms can map to the same inferred Epileptor value.

readouts.name: Regional Epileptor excitability parameter
readouts.interpretation: Regions above the model's critical excitability value are treated as autonomous seizure generators.

variables.name: Regional excitability
variables.description: Epileptor excitability assigned to each parcellated brain region; the approximate critical value is -2.0.

variables.name: Structural connectivity
variables.description: Patient-specific region-to-region coupling derived from diffusion-MRI tractography.

variables.name: SEEG source-to-sensor gain
variables.description: Projection from simulated regional activity to reconstructed intracranial electrode contacts.

variables.name: Stimulation waveform input
variables.description: Time-varying, dimensionless perturbation signal matching the clinically applied stimulus waveform.

findings.statement: Patient-specific virtual seizures reproduced empirical spontaneous-seizure features better than randomized epileptogenic-zone assignments across the tested spatiotemporal metrics.
For stimulated seizures, the patient-specific cohort outperformed randomized twins on most metrics, but seizure-propagation similarity was not significantly different.
In an independent retrospective VEP evaluation, predicted epileptogenic-zone precision was 64% and recall was 44% relative to the clinical definition; precision was higher in seizure-free patients.

assertion.notes: Repository inspected at commit a99c88354015f4c961d49a92c076ed0b675c740b (2025-04-24). Python byte-compilation succeeds, with two non-fatal invalid-escape SyntaxWarnings. End-to-end execution was not attempted because the repository has no dependency manifest or license, does not bundle the EBRAINS patient dataset, and relies on local data paths and The Virtual Brain. The README also names one interictal-generation script that is not present under that exact filename. These limitations constrain reproducibility despite the public source and separately deposited virtual cohort.

selected_evidence.snippet: To address this, we generated and evaluated a cohort of 30 virtual epilepsy patients, using patient-specific anatomical and functional data from 30 real drug-resistant epilepsy patients.

assertion.name: ATM/ATR DNA-damage-response and drug-repurposing ODE model

findings.statement: In the ATM-deficient arm, ATR becomes the principal pathway regulating the modeled cellular response to DNA damage.

value.name: ATM p.Ala2386Glu variant-structure predictions
value.description: Allele-specific structural analyses of homozygous ATM c.7157C>A (p.Ala2386Glu) found in two brothers with variant A-T. Missense3D/PHYRE2 and DynaMut modeled the substitution in the FAT-domain alpha-21 helix against wild-type cryo-EM template PDB 6K9L and produced competing hypotheses: buried-charge structural destabilization or stabilization of the closed, less-active ATM dimer. Patient lymphoblastoid-cell experiments favored the instability branch while showing residual kinase function.
value.notes: No mutant coordinates, prediction outputs, code, or reusable model archive were deposited; PDB 6K9L is the wild-type experimental template, not the p.Ala2386Glu model. The template resolution is 4.27 angstrom. The structural analysis is useful because it is allele-explicit and experimentally checked, but it remains a one-family result and does not model the full A-T spectrum.

value.name: Normative diffusion-perfusion MRI autoencoder
value.description: A seven-layer, fully connected PyTorch autoencoder trained only on healthy pediatric MRI features to detect individual deviations in A-T. Twenty inputs (13 regional diffusion/perfusion features plus seven demographic and volume covariates) are compressed and 13 imaging features are reconstructed. The paper reports a four-dimensional latent layer, whereas the released notebook instantiates five latent units. One hundred controls were used for training and validation, 10 controls for held-out testing, and 16 children with A-T for disease evaluation.

variables.name: Total MRI-feature reconstruction error
variables.description: Per-subject mean-squared error across the 13 reconstructed imaging features; group summaries report the median.

variables.name: Cerebellar gray-matter diffusion reconstruction error
variables.description: Individual deviation in cerebellar gray-matter apparent diffusion coefficient.

variables.name: Cerebellar white-matter diffusion reconstruction error
variables.description: Individual deviation in cerebellar white-matter apparent diffusion coefficient.

value.notes: The MIT-licensed repository is pinned at commit d14295ced27c4cbee3e22db966daed38c40f831e and includes the training/test/A-T combined-feature CSV files plus the analysis notebook; the feature data have no separate data-license file. It does not include trained weights, a dependency manifest, or an environment lock. The notebook expects nine absent split CSV files, saves and loads weights through an author's private Google Drive path, and omits code that constructs several later analysis objects. Its formulas instantiate a five-unit latent layer rather than the four-unit architecture stated in the paper. The committed artifact is therefore not a self-contained replay of the published analysis. The 16-person A-T cohort is small and has no external validation cohort; training controls are younger on average, and exploratory clinical associations were not corrected for multiple testing. This is an individualized anomaly detector, not a longitudinal patient digital twin.

assertion.description: Reconstruction error measures deviations in cerebellar and subcortical MRI diffusion/perfusion features relative to a healthy normative model; it does not simulate the causal degeneration process.
assertion.limitations: The model measures cross-sectional brain-imaging anomalies only. It does not measure peripheral nerves, neuronal loss directly, longitudinal progression, or treatment response, and SHAP associations cannot establish causal inter-regional mechanisms.

readouts.name: Total MRI-feature reconstruction error
readouts.description: Median reconstruction error was 4.5 x 10^-3 in 16 A-T participants and 4.0 x 10^-4 in 10 held-out controls (P=1.5 x 10^-6).

selected_evidence.snippet: A normative deep autoencoder that reconstructs these features was trained on healthy subjects.

assertion.name: Sandefur purinergic model of airway-surface-liquid homeostasis
assertion.description: Systems model coupling epithelial ion and water transport to extracellular ATP and adenosine signaling. Fifteen ODEs represent baseline ASL homeostasis; a 23-equation extension simulates prolonged low-dose P2Y2-agonist delivery.
assertion.model_format: ODE equations and parameters in the article and supplemental material

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reduces CFTR-mediated chloride secretion within a calibrated model of cultured human airway epithelium.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: CF required simultaneous parameter changes in chloride, sodium, and potassium transport; CFTR loss is therefore not an isolated disease arm.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Increased sodium absorption is required with reduced chloride secretion to reproduce the CF epithelial state.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Transport parameters were fitted to cultured epithelia and do not encode patient genotype, airway anatomy, immune responses, or infection.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Predicts the lower resting ASL height in CF and its dependence on chloride secretion, sodium absorption, and extracellular nucleotide metabolism.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: ASL height is modeled in cultured epithelium; extrapolation to spatially heterogeneous intact airways and clinical response is unvalidated.

assertion.name: Bone cell population dynamics model of the remodeling unit
assertion.description: A differential-equation model of autocrine and paracrine signalling between osteoblast and osteoclast lineages at a single remodeling site, solving for cell population dynamics and the resulting change in bone mass. It is the formal counterpart of this entry's Bone Remodeling Imbalance node.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reproduces a single remodeling cycle, self-sustaining cycling, and unstable runaway remodeling from one parameter set, and identifies autocrine regulation of osteoclasts as the parameter that decides which regime the system occupies.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: A single-site abstraction with lumped parameters and no spatial structure, no osteocyte compartment, and no aging or estrogen axis, so it cannot represent the senescence or marrow-lineage nodes in this entry. Its pathological regime was matched to Paget disease rather than to osteoporosis.

assertion.notes: No committed dismech-perturb run exists for this model; it is recorded as published external work, not as an executable model in this repository.

selected_evidence.snippet: Parametric analysis demonstrated that the mode of dynamic behavior in the system depends strongly on the regulation of osteoclasts by autocrine factors, such as transforming growth factor beta.

assertion.name: QCT-based finite element model of the proximal femur
assertion.description: A patient-specific structural model built from a quantitative CT scan of the hip, solving for femoral strength and for the ratio of the load a fall would impose to the strength available to resist it. It is the computational counterpart of this entry's claim that microarchitecture and geometry carry fracture risk that areal BMD alone does not.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Turns the structural deterioration this node describes into a mechanical quantity that prospectively predicts hip fracture, and the load-to-strength ratio stays predictive after adjustment for areal BMD.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Resolves geometry and density at CT scale, so it does not represent trabecular connectivity or cortical porosity directly, and it says nothing about the cellular mechanisms upstream. Validated here in older men; the cohort is not the population most affected.

readouts.name: Load-to-strength ratio adjusted for areal BMD
readouts.interpretation: Retained prediction after BMD adjustment is what shows the model captures structural information beyond density.

selected_evidence.snippet: These results provide insight into hip fracture etiology and demonstrate the ability of FE-based biomechanical analysis of QCT scans to prospectively predict hip fractures in men.

assertion.name: RCC 3D Agent-Based Learning Model
assertion.description: Spatial three-dimensional agent-based simulation of established renal cell carcinoma, immune-cell populations, sex-hormone effects, and ICI or TKI treatment rules. A genetic algorithm evolves synthetic tumor-cell genotypes, while Optuna tunes model parameters against overall-survival and survival-status outcomes from selected ARON registry cases.
assertion.base_model: OncoAgent RCC obesity-paradox agent-based learning model (PMID:33996779)
assertion.model_format: Custom imperative Python/Mesa source (not SBML or CellML); Jupyter Notebook (IPYNB); CSV patient input

variables.name: Patient sex
variables.description: Biological-sex input used to initialize hormone and immune-cell rules.

variables.name: Treatment regimen
variables.description: Model input selecting ICI, TKI, combined ICI plus TKI, or no treatment.

variables.name: Treatment start
variables.description: Simulation step at which the selected treatment begins.

variables.name: Tumor-cell count
variables.description: Number of spatial tumor-cell agents collected during a simulation.

variables.name: Simulated overall survival
variables.description: Number of simulation steps before the modeled stopping outcome.

variables.name: Mean tumor mutation mask
variables.description: Mean binary mutation profile across the simulated tumor-cell population, used to summarize within-model genetic adaptation.

modeled_mechanisms.description: The model simulates expansion or regression of an established RCC tumor-cell population under spatial immune pressure, evolving tumor-cell rules, and ICI or ICI-plus-TKI treatment.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The simulation begins with generic tumor cells and does not model renal epithelial transformation, kidney anatomy, or a specified RCC histology. It was tuned and assessed on the same seven selected cases without a held-out or external cohort. Sex is perfectly confounded with regimen in those cases: all three male records received ICI and all four female records received ICI plus TKI. Immune concentrations were estimated, simulation steps and tumor-count thresholds are not calibrated clinical endpoints, and the synthetic mutation system does not reproduce patient RCC genomes.

readouts.name: Simulated tumor-cell burden trajectory
readouts.description: Tumor-cell counts change over time according to the initialized case, stochastic seed, immune interactions, tumor adaptation, and treatment rules.
readouts.interpretation: This is a model-specific trajectory rather than a validated measure of clinical tumor volume or treatment efficacy.

findings.statement: Female-model runs showed delayed initial responses followed by stronger late immune activation and rapid regression, whereas male-model runs showed steadier early responses but greater modeled tumor resilience.
Parameter tuning used seven RCC records and 26 Optuna trials for each objective; the paper reports lower aggregate prediction MSE and increasingly stable CI, without held-out validation.

assertion.notes: The GitHub repository is pinned at unsigned commit 40220d6c398d90b41971f102acb9f84838982601 (tree acfe9582f716869dc965aad04c11f279a5c13470) and has no tags or releases. Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.18727138 archives software version 1.0.0 as RCC-ALM.zip (SHA-256 4e7c38b570916555fac9fd422f0e5b8d52c5ebd2f8c93a708f3b0dedf4745358), although pyproject.toml calls the package 0.1.0; all 72 archived files are byte-identical to the pinned Git tree. Software Heritage directory swh:1:dir:570c82c75e1f417940762d4d66706f3467df706c contains the matching inner Git-tree directory, but no revision object for the commit resolves, so it preserves deposited content rather than Git history. The repository LICENSE and Zenodo software record are MIT. The upstream ARON-1 dataset is Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13353313 under CC BY 4.0. The repository contains three byte-identical copies of a derived seven-row, 19-column CSV (SHA-256 aef040b2d21069fcdb58aca45a3331fa03c85c2dfadf6b9d5e8bc713cbf1d585), but does not cite that DOI, state data-specific attribution or licensing, or provide the manual selection and conversion procedure. Curator smoke testing installed the requirements under Python 3.13.9, constructed and advanced the 643-agent default model, exercised a small data pipeline, and completed the documented 100-step non-GUI command. That command emits only console traces and does not reproduce a paper result. Reproducibility remains partial: dependencies are not fully pinned or locked; the documented Solara interface fails with the resolved unbounded Starlette version; the built wheel omits required package data and uses incompatible src.* imports outside the checkout; and the analysis notebook has no executed outputs or reference results. There are 83 tuned weights for seven non-held-out cases. The MSE result-loading code mistakenly reloads CI parameters, repeat-count handling is defective, stochastic antigen selection depends on Python hash ordering, and a class-global tumor blood-source list can contaminate repeated runs. The model is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, not a clinically validated patient digital twin. Generic mutation adaptation does not justify linking it to the entry's histologic-and-molecular-subtype node, and it does not encode the PRR15/NF-κB/FDX1 cuproptosis mechanism.

selected_evidence.snippet: An RCC-specific ALM was developed incorporating immune agents (CD8+, NK, Treg, dendritic cells), hormone-sensitive mechanisms, tumor genetic modules, and effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.18727138 archives software version 1.0.0 as RCC-ALM.zip (SHA-256 4e7c38b570916555fac9fd422f0e5b8d52c5ebd2f8c93a708f3b0dedf4745358), although pyproject.toml calls the package 0.1.0; all 72 archived files are byte-identical to the pinned Git tree. Software Heritage directory swh:1:dir:570c82c75e1f417940762d4d66706f3467df706c contains the matching inner Git-tree directory, but no revision object for the commit resolves, so it preserves deposited content rather than Git history. The repository LICENSE and Zenodo software record are MIT. The upstream ARON-1 dataset is Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13353313 under CC BY 4.0. The repository contains three byte-identical copies of a derived seven-row, 19-column CSV (SHA-256 aef040b2d21069fcdb58aca45a3331fa03c85c2dfadf6b9d5e8bc713cbf1d585), but does not cite that DOI, state data-specific attribution or licensing, or provide the manual selection and conversion procedure. Curator smoke testing installed the requirements under Python 3.13.9, constructed and advanced the 643-agent default model, exercised a small data pipeline, and completed the documented 100-step non-GUI command. That command emits only console traces and does not reproduce a paper result. Reproducibility remains partial: dependencies are not fully pinned or locked; the documented Solara interface fails with the resolved unbounded Starlette version; the built wheel omits required package data and uses incompatible src.* imports outside the checkout; and the analysis notebook has no executed outputs or reference results. There are 83 tuned weights for seven non-held-out cases. The MSE result-loading code mistakenly reloads CI parameters, repeat-count handling is defective, stochastic antigen selection depends on Python hash ordering, and a class-global tumor blood-source list can contaminate repeated runs. The model is exploratory and hypothesis-generating, not a clinically validated patient digital twin. Generic mutation adaptation does not justify linking it to the entry's histologic-and-molecular-subtype node, and it does not encode the PRR15/NF-κB/FDX1 cuproptosis mechanism.

assertion.name: Patient-Specific CML Tumor-NK Treatment-Cessation ODE Model
assertion.description: Patient-calibrated three-state ordinary differential-equation model of active, TKI-sensitive CML tumor cells; reversible quiescent, niche-bound and TKI-insensitive tumor cells; and immune effector cells represented using cytolytic NK-cell data. TKI exposure is a time-varying tumor-kill term, while immune control incorporates density-dependent searching, handling, recharging, and tumor-suppressed effector function and recruitment.
assertion.model_format: Wolfram Notebook (.nb); Wolfram Language (.m/.wl); CSV/TXT inputs; PDF outputs

variables.name: Active TKI-sensitive tumor cells
variables.description: Proliferating CML tumor-cell state (paper notation T; deposited-code identifier Y) subject to TKI and immune-mediated depletion.

variables.name: Quiescent niche-bound tumor cells
variables.description: Reversible non-proliferating tumor-cell state (paper notation T_N; deposited-code identifier X) that is insensitive to TKI in the model.

variables.name: Immune effector-cell abundance
variables.description: Effector-cell state (paper notation E; deposited-code identifier Z) calibrated using absolute cytolytic NK-cell counts from peripheral blood.

variables.name: Tumor-dependent NK-cell functionality
variables.description: Dimensionless functional response (paper h(T); deposited code h[Y]) fitted from normalized percentages of CD107a-positive NK cells across tumor burdens.

variables.name: BCR-ABL1/ABL1 molecular burden
variables.description: Clinical percentage used as the observed proxy for active tumor-cell burden.

variables.name: Functional immune-cell abundance
variables.description: Product of immune effector-cell abundance and modeled NK-cell functionality, evaluated in the deposited code as h[Y[t]]*Z[t].

variables.name: Molecular-relapse probability
variables.description: Fraction of the 100 retained patient-specific parameter fits whose simulated tumor burden exceeds MR3 at 12, 24, or 36 months after treatment cessation.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Active CML tumor cells proliferate, transition reversibly to a quiescent niche-bound state, and are depleted by lumped TKI and NK-cell effects. Longitudinal BCR-ABL1/ABL1 molecular burden calibrates the active tumor-cell trajectory for individual patients.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The generic active and quiescent tumor compartments do not reproduce the node's BCR-ABL1-driven myeloid-progenitor differentiation, granulocytic expansion, marrow anatomy, or hypercellularity. BCR-ABL1/ABL1 is a tumor-load proxy rather than an explicit fusion or kinase-signaling state; TKI action is a time-switched kill term. The model omits kinase-domain resistance, RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT, JAK-STAT, apoptosis signaling, genomic evolution, and blast-phase progression. Patient-specific tumor-growth and immune-kill parameters are non-identifiable from full-dose data alone, and the study has no held-out, external, or prospective clinical validation cohort. The published and deposited m_K search bounds also differ, so the fitted immune-kill contribution is not exactly reproducible from the Methods alone.

readouts.name: BCR-ABL1/ABL1 tumor-burden trajectory
readouts.description: Simulated active tumor-cell abundance converted to the clinical BCR-ABL1/ABL1 percentage and fitted across full-dose, half-dose, and treatment-cessation intervals.
readouts.interpretation: A patient-calibrated molecular-burden trajectory, not a direct measure of marrow myeloid proliferation or lineage output.

readouts.name: Patient-specific molecular-relapse probability
readouts.description: Fraction of retained fits predicting tumor burden above MR3 at 12, 24, or 36 months after TKI cessation.
readouts.interpretation: An ensemble-derived model probability evaluated against a full-trajectory best-fit reference, not a prospectively validated recurrence probability.

findings.statement: Full-dose tumor trajectories alone did not resolve treatment-cessation behavior; including the one-year half-dose response increased internal prediction quality, with a further increase after six post-cessation months.
In the model ensembles, a loss of more than 20% of functional immune-cell abundance after dose reduction was strongly associated with molecular relapse.

assertion.notes: The final five-author publication is PMID:41102232. Its code and data point to Zenodo record 13939516, created for the 2024 preprint; its UI shows v1, but its metadata has no semantic version. The record has concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13939515 and uses the bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2024.10.10.617526 as its record DOI; a putative version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13939516 does not resolve. The single code and data.zip file is 135,806,838 bytes (Zenodo-reported MD5 327afa8fc9df02a01c4c4318cfe04aaf; locally computed SHA-256 6656ac6fb83cf893ca33367b0f39b70829a80c72c452dbb02ea5de4c2d1099a4), passes ZIP integrity checks, and contains 398 files: ten ordered Mathematica notebooks, generated 4_model_Code.m, four input-data files, 16 precomputed Wolfram outputs, 57 manuscript figures, 308 patient-fit PDFs, a DOCX README, and .DS_Store. Zenodo metadata declares CC BY 4.0, but the ZIP has no embedded license; the final article is separately CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The author environment is Mathematica 14.1 on an ARM Mac and uses built-ins without an environment lock. A Mathics compatibility smoke test parsed and loaded the generated package and bundled serialized cohort metadata (n=8 Hughes; n=75 DESTINY), then constructed the three ODEs and default initial conditions. Per-patient Hughes evaluation hit Mathics Association/string incompatibilities, Mathics cannot execute the required multivariate NDSolve workflow, and licensed Mathematica was unavailable, so full numerical and figure reproduction was not verified. The notebooks also depend on NotebookDirectory, $FrontEndSession, and PDF export, while solver method, numerical precision, and kernel count are unpinned. Fresh execution on a case-sensitive system also requires correcting data_destiny.csv to the deposited data_Destiny.csv and out_patients_hughes.wl to out_patients_Hughes.wl; the README misnames the final notebook. The complete million-combination search over three parameters is documented as about seven hours on an M3 Mac, while the fixed-parameter 10,000-pair workflow takes under 30 minutes; precomputed outputs permit figure inspection without recomputation. A material methods/code discrepancy affects the immune-kill parameter m_K: the paper specifies a search range of [0,1], while the deposited code searches [0,4]; 2,159 of 7,500 retained million-combination fits across 29 of 75 patients exceed 1 (maximum 3.99966), as do 200 of 7,500 fixed-c_K full-course fits for patients 60 and 69 (maximum 2.89195). The deposited code and results therefore do not exactly implement the published bound, and interpretation requires author clarification. The README also mislabels fitted p_T tuples as p_E. The deposited Hughes data have ten patients, and the workflow hard-codes eight without recording the selection rationale; the paper describes its modeled subset as the eight patients on full TKI dose. The DESTINY deposit has 78 patients (75 selected plus three extras), not the full 174 described in the paper, so the original selection cannot be rerun from this archive alone. For each selected patient, simplified fixed-c_K analyses retain the 100 best fits from 10,000 (p_T,m_K) pairs, while the full analysis retains 100 from one million (p_T,m_K,c_K) combinations. DESTINY has no NK trajectories: NK-number/suppression and NK-function parameters are fixed to population-summary values derived from the eight Hughes patients, while patient-specific p_T and m_K (and c_K in the full three-parameter analysis) are calibrated only from tumor-load data. Deposited internal ROC AUCs for relapse at 12/24/36 months rise from 0.57/0.53/0.53 using full-dose data to 0.79/0.73/0.71 through half dose and 0.92/0.95/0.92 after six post-cessation months, but the reference true scenario is the best complete-trajectory fit, not observed held-out outcomes. This is an artifact-backed, partially reproducible proof-of-concept for patient-calibrated tumor-immune dynamics, not a clinically validated digital twin. The model does not justify links to upstream BCR-ABL1 signaling, apoptosis resistance, genomic instability, or blast crisis.

selected_evidence.snippet: Starting from classical ecological modeling concepts, which allow to explicitly account for immune interactions at the cellular level, we incorporate time-course data on natural killer (NK) cell number, function, and their tumor-induced suppression into our general model of CML treatment.

value.name: Multiscale kinetic model of leucine-stimulated muscle protein metabolism
value.description: A mechanistic kinetic model linking leucine ingestion and absorption, insulin secretion, intracellular mTORC1-p70S6K signalling, and muscle protein synthesis and breakdown in human skeletal muscle. It was extended to represent anabolic resistance: the ageing-related impairments were parameterised individually and in combination, and a virtual population was classified as anabolic-sensitive or anabolic-resistant. The model was then used to simulate single-target and multi-target interventions.
value.notes: The stimulus represented is protein feeding. Resistance exercise and mechanical loading are not in the model, so it says nothing directly about the Blunted Load-Induced mTORC1 Signalling node; the authors note that exercise enhances muscle sensitivity to protein feeding, which is the interaction a loading extension would need to capture.

assertion.description: Reproduces the reduced protein-synthetic response to feeding in older adults, and only when several impairments are combined.
assertion.limitations: Calibrated against two small human feeding studies, developed from male data only, feeding-only, and focused on protein turnover rather than strength or function.

divergences.description: Mechanical loading and the exercise arm of anabolic resistance are outside the model boundary; only the leucine-feeding stimulus is represented.

Parameters come from studies in men. Sex differences in ageing-related protein metabolism are reported in some studies but not others, so the results may not transfer to older women, who are the majority of sarcopenia trial participants.

The anabolic-resistant phenotype was evaluated against two small cohort studies, so the size of each simulated impairment is weakly constrained given how variable anabolic resistance is between individuals.

selected_evidence.snippet: Second, the model was developed using data from males.

assertion.name: Human SLC25A20 conformational models and molecular dynamics
assertion.description: AlphaFold2/ColabFold models of cytoplasmic-open and matrix-open human SLC25A20, molecular dynamics and substrate docking explore conformational asymmetry and binding determinants. Structural analysis suggests explanations for Asp231His and Ala281Val. The reported simulations do not directly quantify patient-mutant transport or clinical phenotype.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Molecular structural proxies inform the normal transport architecture and interpretations of pathogenic substitutions.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Simulations and docking of modeled conformations do not directly measure deficient substrate transport. Clinical effects of mutations are inferred from their positions and interactions.

divergences.description: Salt-bridge persistence, helix packing and docked substrate contacts are structural proxies for transport activity.
The disease variants are interpreted from carrier structures; the reported simulations are not direct functional tests of variant-specific transport deficiency.
Cellular energy metabolism, tissue injury and clinical outcomes lie outside the isolated transporter model.

findings.statement: Predicted Asp231His effects involve matrix salt-bridge interactions; Ala281Val may perturb H5/H6 packing. Experimental mutant-transport confirmation is not supplied by this modeling study.

selected_evidence.snippet: the data suggest that the pathogenic mutation Asp231His perturbs the matrix salt bridge Asp231-Lys35 and/or the Asp231-Arg178 interactions, which are involved in the stability of the c- and m-state.

assertion.name: Fabbri-Severi human sinoatrial node cell model with HCN4 mutation-induced I_f changes
assertion.description: A published in-silico risk-stratification study of SSS2. In-vitro biophysical data for HCN4 loss-of-function alleles were used to compute the charge carried by I_f during diastolic depolarization of a prerecorded human sinoatrial node action potential, and that quantity was used to drive the Fabbri-Severi model of a human sinoatrial node pacemaker cell. It is the computational counterpart of the funny-current node in this entry: it makes the qualitative claim (less diastolic I_f, slower firing) quantitative and allele-specific.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Reduced Funny Current and Slowed Diastolic Depolarization
modeled_mechanisms.description: The simulated beating rate of the human sinoatrial node cell model tracks the computed diastolic I_f charge very closely, and the same quantity correlates strongly with the resting and minimum heart rates observed in carriers of the corresponding HCN4 mutations.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The correlation with clinical heart rate is strong but not deterministic, the analysis is restricted to the subset of HCN4 alleles with both quantitative clinical and in-vitro data, and the authors state that a translational perspective remains to be established.

findings.statement: The diastolic funny-current charge computed by action-potential clamp predicts both the simulated pacemaker rate of a human sinoatrial node cell model and the resting or minimum heart rate of HCN4 mutation carriers, making it a candidate risk-stratification measure for HCN4 loss-of-function sinus bradycardia.

assertion.name: Lu stochastic kinetic model of HbS polymerization and erythrocyte sickling
assertion.description: Patient- and organ-parameterized model coupling oxygen-dependent HbS solubility, homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation, fiber growth, and a mechanical criterion for red-cell sickling. Inputs include oxygen tension, deoxygenation time, temperature, cell volume, hemoglobin concentration, and hemoglobin composition.
assertion.model_format: Stochastic kinetic equations and parameters in the article and supplementary materials

modeled_mechanisms.description: Simulates oxygen-dependent HbS nucleation and fiber growth using classical nucleation theory and chemical rate laws.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: HbS nucleus structure is not experimentally known, so the nucleation barrier and related prefactors rely on approximations and fitted values.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Converts simulated intracellular fiber-bundle growth into sickling time and the predicted fraction of sickled erythrocytes.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Predictions depend strongly on patient-specific hemoglobin distributions, composition, and mean cell volume; missing inputs were sometimes replaced by assumed population values, and oxygen tension was modeled as spatially uniform.

variables.name: Oxygen tension
variables.description: Initial and final intracellular oxygen partial pressure during deoxygenation

variables.name: Mean corpuscular volume
variables.description: Patient-specific erythrocyte volume

variables.name: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
variables.description: Intracellular total hemoglobin concentration

variables.name: Hemoglobin composition
variables.description: Mole fractions of HbS, HbF, HbA, and other hemoglobin variants

variables.name: Nucleation delay time
variables.description: Delay before steady homogeneous HbS nucleation

variables.name: Sickled red-cell fraction
variables.description: Fraction of modeled cells meeting the fiber-based sickling criterion

findings.statement: Model sensitivity identified HbS solubility, the nucleation-rate prefactor, and oxygen affinity as dominant determinants of polymerization.
The model was checked against prior in-vivo and in-vitro sickling data and produced drug-effect estimates consistent with recent screening assays.

assertion.notes: Curated directly from the paper and supplementary equations; no exact code repository was identified. This is not a clinically validated digital twin: patient-specific inputs improve individual simulations, but prospective prognosis and dosing claims require further experimental validation.

selected_evidence.snippet: Thus, we developed a kinetic model based on the classical nucleation theory to examine the effectiveness of potential anti-sickling drug candidates.

assertion.name: Zheng multiscale QSP model of autologous gene therapy
assertion.description: Deterministic ordinary-differential-equation model coupling hematopoietic stem-cell engraftment, erythroid differentiation, red-cell turnover, globin assembly, and oxygen-regulated erythropoiesis. Healthy and SCD parameterizations are extended with myeloablative preconditioning and transplantation of CD34-positive cells expressing an anti-sickling gamma-globin.
assertion.model_format: ODE equations and parameters in the article and supporting information

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reproduces the shortened red-cell lifespan and compensatory erythropoietic state used to distinguish the SCD and healthy steady states.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Hemolysis is represented through a fixed mean red-cell lifespan rather than explicit intravascular and extravascular destruction mechanisms.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Simulates replacement of HbS-containing cells by longer-lived transduced cells expressing an anti-sickling hemoglobin after autologous gene therapy.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model predicts hemoglobin composition and a non-sickled-cell fraction but does not explicitly simulate HbS nucleation, fiber growth, membrane deformation, vaso-occlusion, or organ injury.

variables.description: Number of autologous progenitor cells infused after preconditioning

variables.name: Long-term hematopoietic stem-cell fraction
variables.description: Fraction of the infused dose capable of stable long-term engraftment

variables.name: Mean vector copy number
variables.description: Model proxy for the fraction of infused cells carrying the therapeutic vector

variables.name: Preconditioning depletion
variables.description: Fractional depletion of endogenous hematopoietic progenitor pools

variables.name: Anti-sickling hemoglobin
variables.description: Peripheral-blood concentration of the modeled therapeutic hemoglobin

variables.name: Transduced red blood cells
variables.description: Circulating red cells derived from transduced progenitors

findings.statement: Simulated reconstitution is biphasic: short-lived progenitors generate an early wave of transduced red cells, while long-term stem-cell engraftment sustains later production.
Initial transduced-cell dose and myeloablative preconditioning intensity were the strongest positive determinants of modeled long-term outcome.

assertion.notes: Curated from the publication and supporting equations; no exact deposited implementation was identified. Important assumptions include deterministic population averages, at most one vector copy per cell, fixed fractional progenitor depletion, immediate marrow homing, omission of non-erythroid hematopoiesis and iron/heme handling, and empirical oxygen feedback.

selected_evidence.snippet: We used ordinary differential equations to model RBC production from progenitor cells in the bone marrow, and hemoglobin assembly from its constituent globin monomers.

assertion.name: Aston2018 HCV Within-Host Viral-Dynamics Model
assertion.description: Deterministic three-state ordinary differential-equation model of healthy hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and circulating HCV viral load in a well-mixed liver compartment. It represents hepatocyte regeneration and death, infection, virion production and clearance, and treatment-adjusted infection and virion-production rates.
assertion.model_software: MATLAB for publication fitting; COPASI for the BioModels model and fitted variants
assertion.model_format: SBML Level 2 Version 4 (main PVR parameterization); COPASI CPS scenario variants; SED-ML Level 1 Version 4 / COMBINE OMEX

variables.name: Healthy hepatocyte concentration
variables.description: Latent model-scaled concentration of uninfected hepatocytes; it was not observed in the fitted clinical viral-load datasets.

variables.name: Infected hepatocyte concentration
variables.description: Latent model-scaled concentration of infected hepatocytes inferred from viral-load fitting rather than measured in the clinical datasets.

variables.name: HCV viral load
variables.description: Observable model state fitted to treatment-period HCV RNA measurements.

variables.name: Stem-cell hepatocyte generation rate
variables.description: Rate parameter for generation of healthy hepatocytes in proportion to infected hepatocytes.

variables.name: Treatment-adjusted infection rate
variables.description: SBML parameter for the treatment-adjusted rate at which virions infect healthy hepatocytes.

variables.name: Treatment-adjusted virion-production rate
variables.description: Rate of virion production by infected hepatocytes after the modeled treatment effect.

modeled_mechanisms.target: HCV genome replication and early viremia
modeled_mechanisms.description: The model explicitly couples healthy-hepatocyte infection, infected-cell loss, virion production, and viral clearance, and fits the viral-load state to human treatment-response profiles.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The model is deterministic and well mixed, with only healthy hepatocytes, infected hepatocytes, and virions. Hepatocyte states are latent and were not measured in the fitted datasets; aggregate death-rate terms replace immune-mediated injury. Viral genotype and evolution, interferon signaling, immune-cell responses, inflammation, fibrosis, and cancer are absent. Four treatment profiles were fitted in-sample without held-out or prospective validation, and substantially different parameter sets can produce similar fits.

readouts.name: HCV viral-load trajectory
readouts.target: HCV genome replication and early viremia
readouts.description: Time course of state V, fitted on the logarithmic scale to viral-load measurements obtained during treatment.
readouts.interpretation: Captures partial-response, breakthrough, null-response, and triphasic profile shapes but is not a prospectively validated individual treatment prediction.

findings.statement: The same three-state ODE structure was fitted to partial virologic response, breakthrough, null-response, and triphasic treatment-period viral-load profiles.

With stem-cell hepatocyte generation set to zero, the model has uninfected, infected, and pure-infection steady-state branches; adding stem-cell generation unfolds the pure-infection bifurcation into one valid infected branch with a limit point.

assertion.notes: BioModels entry BIOMD0000000713 (internal submission MODEL1808280002) is manually curated; this record pins public revision 9 at https://www.biomodels.org/services/download/get-files/MODEL1808280002/9/MODEL1808280002.9.omex. The revision-9 COMBINE archive retrieved for curator testing was 83,278 bytes with SHA-256 5ca8ec25248d053f4dc52374658df7fc403ea1c4fa4a9141ca93bd0b600712c8, and its main PVR.xml file has SHA-256 b8d62ff28623b18ba31fd59a39a3f5bbd799a0fef9601a5a0f435d5c722cf3b3. BioModels distributes the model under CC0; the archive itself contains no separate license file. PVR.cps, Breakthrough.cps, NullResponse.cps, and Triphasic.cps are distinct parameter and initial-condition variants of the same three-species, nine-reaction structure. Under Python 3.13.9 with COPASI 4.46.300 and basiCO 0.86, all four CPS files loaded and simulated; the PVR SBML and CPS trajectories agreed to a maximum relative difference below 1.03e-7 under matched LSODA settings and reproduced the archived Figure 12(a) result. The standardized workflow is incomplete: every SED-ML file references PVR.xml without model changes, so the named Breakthrough, NullResponse, and Triphasic SED-ML files do not encode their corresponding CPS parameterizations; Breakthrough.sedml and NullResponse.sedml are byte-identical. The stored Triphasic CPS time-course settings are internally inconsistent (19 steps of 3.333333333 days with a declared duration of 60 days), and current COPASI runs to 63.333 days unless the step size is forced to 60/19. BioSimulators archive validation completes with unit/modeling warnings, but the standardized COPASI archive runner hung after task start in the curator environment while direct COPASI execution succeeded. libSBML reports no parse errors, with 17 unit/modeling-practice warnings including eight parameters without declared units. The archive hash is a retrieval snapshot because BioModels can regenerate container packaging; the revision and main-file hash are the stronger content pins. The original MATLAB fit estimated ten parameters and initial values by least squares on log viral load. Raw fitting data and fitting code are not deposited, COPASI parameter-estimation and validation sets are empty, and the paper warns that substantially different parameters give similar fits. The clinical profiles predate modern direct-acting antiviral regimens; direct-acting antiviral effects are discussed as parameter hypotheses rather than validated against DAA-treated cohorts. The model does not justify links to Chronic Inflammation and Fibrosis, Immune Evasion, or Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development.

The model does not justify links to Chronic Inflammation and Fibrosis, Immune Evasion, or Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development.

value.name: Bi-atrial in silico Fabry arrhythmia model
value.description: Physiological bi-atrial simulation model parameterized with GLA p.N215S iPSC-derived atrial cardiomyocyte changes to evaluate P-wave morphology and atrial fibrillation vulnerability in early Fabry cardiac disease.

variables.name: P-wave morphology
variables.description: Simulated ECG morphology output linked to early Fabry cardiomyopathy.

variables.name: Atrial fibrillation vulnerability
variables.description: Simulated arrhythmia susceptibility output from atrial cellular remodeling.

assertion.description: The model translates cellular action-potential and calcium-handling changes into atrial ECG and arrhythmia outputs.
assertion.limitations: The cellular remodeling this link points at is the model's input, not its result: the bi-atrial simulations were built with the cellular changes measured in the p.N215S induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes already imposed as parameter changes. So the model offers no independent support that Fabry atrial cardiomyocytes remodel, and it is linked here for the forward step it does add, from those cellular changes to organ-level P-wave morphology and atrial fibrillation vulnerability. That step is validated by resemblance between the simulated P-wave change and the change seen in early Fabry cardiomyopathy, which is a qualitative agreement rather than a fit to individual patient recordings.

divergences.description: Neither alpha-galactosidase A deficiency nor globotriaosylceramide accumulation is represented. The remodeling enters the model as prescribed ionic and calcium-handling parameter values taken from the cellular experiments, so it is imposed phenomenologically rather than arising from the enzymatic lesion that causes it.

The imposed cellular changes derive from one genome-edited p.N215S induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte line. They are not calibrated against Fabry atrial myocardium, and the simulated P-wave output is compared with the clinical pattern in early Fabry cardiomyopathy rather than with recordings from the donors of those cells.

The parameterization represents the late-onset p.N215S genotype. This entry covers the whole Fabry spectrum, and the model does not speak to atrial arrhythmia vulnerability under classic null alleles.
